1.17.m: Fasting on the twelfth day of the bright fortnight in the month of Āśvina, / Pure, he should devoutly bathe Padmanābha with milk.

1.17.s:
namaste padmanābhāya homaṃ kuyārtsvaśaktitaḥ /
tilabrīhiyavājyaiśca pūjayecca vidhānataḥ //
1.17.d:
नमस्ते पद्मनाभाय होमं कुयार्त्स्वशक्तितः ।
तिलब्रीहियवाज्यैश्च पूजयेच्च विधानतः ॥
1.17.m: With: ‘Obeisance to you, O Padmanābha’, he should perform fire oblation according to his capacity / With sesamum, paddy, barley, and ghee, and worship him according to rule.

1.17.s:
jāmaraṃ niśi nirvartya punaḥ pūjāṃ samācaret /
dadyādviprāya kuḍavaṃ madhunastu sadakṣiṇam //
1.17.d:
जामरं निशि निर्वर्त्य पुनः पूजां समाचरेत् ।
दद्याद्विप्राय कुडवं मधुनस्तु सदक्षिणम् ॥
1.17.m: Having kept a night-vigil, he should perform worship again, / And give to a brāhmaṇa a kuḍava of honey along with a sacrificial fee, [saying]:

1.17.s:
padmanābhagha namastubhyaṃ sarvalokapitāmaha /
madhudānena suprīto bhavasarvasukhapradaḥ //
1.17.d:
पद्मनाभघ नमस्तुभ्यं सर्वलोकपितामह ।
मधुदानेन सुप्रीतो भवसर्वसुखप्रदः ॥
1.17.m: ‘O Padmanābha, obeisance to you, grandfather of all the worlds! / Be exceedingly pleased by this gift of honey, and grant all happiness!’

1.17.s:
evaṃ yaḥ kurute bhaktyā padmanābhavrataṃ sudhīḥ /
brahmamedhasahasrasya phalamānpoti niścitam //
1.17.d:
एवं यः कुरुते भक्त्या पद्मनाभव्रतं सुधीः ।
ब्रह्ममेधसहस्रस्य फलमान्पोति निश्चितम् ॥
1.17.m: The wise person who thus performs the Padmanābha vow with devotion, / Certainly obtains the fruit of a thousand Brahmamedha sacrifices.

1.17.s:
dvādaśyāṃ kārtike śukle upavāsī jitendriyaḥ /
kṣīreṇākaḍhakamānena dandhā vājyena tāvatā //
1.17.d:
द्वादश्यां कार्तिके शुक्ले उपवासी जितेन्द्रियः ।
क्षीरेणाकढकमानेन दन्धा वाज्येन तावता ॥
1.17.m: On the twelfth day of the bright fortnight in Kārtika, fasting with senses restrained, / [He should bathe him] with a measure of an āḍhaka of milk, or with that much curds or ghee,

1.17.s:
namo dāmodarāyeti snāpayedbhaktibhāvataḥ /
aṣṭottaraśataṃ hutvā maghvājyāktatilāhutīḥ //
1.17.d:
नमो दामोदरायेति स्नापयेद्भक्तिभावतः ।
अष्टोत्तरशतं हुत्वा मघ्वाज्याक्ततिलाहुतीः ॥
1.17.m: Devoutly bathing him with: ‘Obeisance to Dāmodara’. / Having offered one hundred and eight oblations of sesamum anointed with honey and ghee,

1.17.s:
jāgaraṃ niyataḥ kuryāttrikālārcanatatparaḥ /
prātaḥ saṃpūjayeddevaṃ padmapuṣpairmanoramaiḥ //
1.17.d:
जागरं नियतः कुर्यात्त्रिकालार्चनतत्परः ।
प्रातः संपूजयेद्देवं पद्मपुष्पैर्मनोरमैः ॥
1.17.m: He should keep a vigil with self-restraint, intent on worship at the three junctures of the day. / In the morning, he should worship the god with charming lotus flowers.

1.17.s:
punaraṣṭottaraśataṃ juhuyātsaghṛtai stilaiḥ /
pañcabhakṣyayutaṃ cānnaṃ dadyādviprāya bhaktitaḥ //
1.17.d:
पुनरष्टोत्तरशतं जुहुयात्सघृतै स्तिलैः ।
पञ्चभक्ष्ययुतं चान्नं दद्याद्विप्राय भक्तितः ॥
1.17.m: He should again offer one hundred and eight oblations with sesamum accompanied by ghee, / And devoutly give food accompanied by the five kinds of delicacies to a brāhmaṇa, [saying]:

1.17.s:
dāmodara jagannātha sarvakāraṇakāraṇa /
trāhimāṃ kṛpayā deva śāraṇāgatapālakaḥ //
1.17.d:
दामोदर जगन्नाथ सर्वकारणकारण ।
त्राहिमां कृपया देव शारणागतपालकः ॥
1.17.m: ‘O Dāmodara, Lord of the world, cause of all causes, / Protect me through your compassion, O God who protects those who take refuge!’

1.17.s:
anena dattvā dānaṃ ca śrotriyāya kuṭumbine /
dakṣiṇāñca yathāśaktyā brāhmaṇāṃśvāpi bhojayet //
1.17.d:
अनेन दत्त्वा दानं च श्रोत्रियाय कुटुम्बिने ।
दक्षिणाञ्च यथाशक्त्या ब्राह्मणांश्वापि भोजयेत् ॥
1.17.m: Having made this gift to a Vedic scholar who has a family, / And given a sacrificial fee according to his capacity, he should also feed brāhmaṇas.

1.17.s:
evaṅkṛtvā vrataṃ samyagaśrīyādvūndhubhiḥ saha /
aśvamegha sahasrāṇāṃ dviguṇaṃ phalamaśnute //
1.17.d:
एवङ्कृत्वा व्रतं सम्यगश्रीयाद्वून्धुभिः सह ।
अश्वमेघ सहस्राणां द्विगुणं फलमश्नुते ॥
1.17.m: Having properly performed this vow, he should eat together with his kinsmen; / He attains twice the fruit of a thousand horse sacrifices.

1.17.s:
evaṃ kuryādvratī yastu dvādaśīvratamuttamam /
saṃvatsaraṃ muniśreṣṭha sa yāti parama padam //
1.17.d:
एवं कुर्याद्व्रती यस्तु द्वादशीव्रतमुत्तमम् ।
संवत्सरं मुनिश्रेष्ठ स याति परम पदम् ॥
1.17.m: The observer of the vow who thus performs this excellent Dvādaśī vow / For a full year, O best of sages, goes to the supreme abode.

1.17.s:
ekamāse dvimāse vāyaḥ kuryādbhaktitatparaḥ /
tattatphalamavānpoti prānpoti ca hareḥ padam //
1.17.d:
एकमासे द्विमासे वायः कुर्याद्भक्तितत्परः ।
तत्तत्फलमवान्पोति प्रान्पोति च हरेः पदम् ॥
1.17.m: He who, intent on devotion, performs it for one month or two months / Obtains their respective fruits and attains the abode of Hari.

1.17.s:
pūrṇaṃ saṃvatsaraṃ kṛtvā kuryādudyāpanaṃ vratī /
mārgaśīrṣāsite pakṣe dvādaśyāṃ ca munīśvara //
1.17.d:
पूर्णं संवत्सरं कृत्वा कुर्यादुद्यापनं व्रती ।
मार्गशीर्षासिते पक्षे द्वादश्यां च मुनीश्वर ॥
1.17.m: Having completed a full year, the observer of the vow should perform the concluding rite / On the twelfth day of the dark fortnight of Mārgaśīrṣa, O lord of sages.

1.17.s:
snātvā prātaryathācāraṃ dantadhāvanapūrvakam /
śuklamālyāmbaradharaḥ śuklagandhānulepanaḥ //
1.17.d:
स्नात्वा प्रातर्यथाचारं दन्तधावनपूर्वकम् ।
शुक्लमाल्याम्बरधरः शुक्लगन्धानुलेपनः ॥
1.17.m: Having bathed in the morning according to custom, preceded by brushing his teeth, / Wearing white garlands and garments, and anointed with white fragrant paste,

1.17.s:
maṇḍapaṃ kārayeddivyaṃ caturastraṃ suśībhanam /
ghaṇṭācāmarasaṃyuktaṃ kiṅkiṇīravaśobhitam //
1.17.d:
मण्डपं कारयेद्दिव्यं चतुरस्त्रं सुशीभनम् ।
घण्टाचामरसंयुक्तं किङ्किणीरवशोभितम् ॥
1.17.m: He should cause a splendid, four-cornered, very beautiful pavilion to be made, / Provided with bells and chowries, and adorned with the sound of small bells,

1.17.s:
alaṅkṛtaṃ puṣpamālyairvitānaghvajarājitān /
chāditaṃ śuklavastreṇa dīpamālāvibhūṣitam //
1.17.d:
अलङ्कृतं पुष्पमाल्यैर्वितानघ्वजराजितान् ।
छादितं शुक्लवस्त्रेण दीपमालाविभूषितम् ॥
1.17.m: Decorated with flower garlands, resplendent with canopies and banners, / Covered with a white cloth, and adorned with rows of lamps.

1.17.s:
tanmadhye sarvatobhadraṃ kuryātsamyagalaṅkṛtam /
tasyoparinyasetkumbhāndvādaśāmbuprapūritān //
1.17.d:
तन्मध्ये सर्वतोभद्रं कुर्यात्सम्यगलङ्कृतम् ।
तस्योपरिन्यसेत्कुम्भान्द्वादशाम्बुप्रपूरितान् ॥
1.17.m: In the middle of it, he should make a well-adorned sarvatobhadra diagram; / Upon it he should place twelve water-jars completely filled with water.

1.17.s:
ekena śulkavanastreṇa samyaksaṃśodhitena ca /
sarvānācchādayetkumbhānpañcaratnasamanvitān //
1.17.d:
एकेन शुल्कवनस्त्रेण सम्यक्संशोधितेन च ।
सर्वानाच्छादयेत्कुम्भान्पञ्चरत्नसमन्वितान् ॥
1.17.m: With a single, thoroughly cleansed white cloth, / He should cover all the jars containing the five gems.

1.17.s:
lakṣmīnārāyaṇaṃ devaṃ kārayedbhaktimānvratī /
henmā vā rājatenāpi tathā tāmreṇa vā dvijā //
1.17.d:
लक्ष्मीनारायणं देवं कारयेद्भक्तिमान्व्रती ।
हेन्मा वा राजतेनापि तथा ताम्रेण वा द्विजा ॥
1.17.m: The devoted vow-keeper should have an image of God Lakṣmīnārāyaṇa made, / Either of gold, or of silver, or also of copper, O twice-born,

1.17.s:
sthāpayetpratimāṃ tāṃ ca kumbhopari susaṃyamī /
tanmūlyaṃ vā dvijaśreṣṭha kāñcanaṃ ca svaśaktitaḥ //
1.17.d:
स्थापयेत्प्रतिमां तां च कुम्भोपरि सुसंयमी ।
तन्मूल्यं वा द्विजश्रेष्ठ काञ्चनं च स्वशक्तितः ॥
1.17.m: And being well-restrained, he should install that image upon the jars; / Or, O best of twice-borns, he should place gold of its value, according to his capacity.

1.17.s:
sarvavrateṣu matimānvittaśāṭhyaṃ vivarja yet /
yadi kuryātkṣayaṃ yānti tasyāyurddhanasaṃpadaḥ //
1.17.d:
सर्वव्रतेषु मतिमान्वित्तशाठ्यं विवर्ज येत् ।
यदि कुर्यात्क्षयं यान्ति तस्यायुर्द्धनसंपदः ॥
1.17.m: In all observances, the wise person should avoid stinginess regarding wealth. / If he should commit it, his lifespan, wealth, and prosperity go to ruin.

1.17.s:
anantaśāyinaṃ devaṃ nārāyaṇamanāmayaṭam /
pañcāmṛtena prathamaṃ snāpayedbhaktisaṃyutaḥ //
1.17.d:
अनन्तशायिनं देवं नारायणमनामयटम् ।
पञ्चामृतेन प्रथमं स्नापयेद्भक्तिसंयुतः ॥
1.17.m: Endowed with devotion, one should first bathe the imperishable God Nārāyaṇa, / who reclines on Ananta, with the five nectars.

1.17.s:
nāṃmabhiḥ keśavādyaiśca hyupacārānmakalpayet /
rātrau jāgaraṇaṃ kuryātpurāṇaśravaṇādibhaghiḥ //
1.17.d:
नांमभिः केशवाद्यैश्च ह्युपचारान्मकल्पयेत् ।
रात्रौ जागरणं कुर्यात्पुराणश्रवणादिभघिः ॥
1.17.m: And one should arrange the offerings with the names beginning with Keśava. / At night one should keep vigil by listening to the Purāṇas and other such means.

1.17.s:
jitanidro bhavetsamyaksopavāso jitendriyaḥ /
trikālamarcayeddevaṃ yathāvibhavavistaram //
1.17.d:
जितनिद्रो भवेत्सम्यक्सोपवासो जितेन्द्रियः ।
त्रिकालमर्चयेद्देवं यथाविभवविस्तरम् ॥
1.17.m: Having conquered sleep, fasting, and with senses restrained, / one should worship the God at the three junctions of the day according to the extent of one's wealth.

1.17.s:
tataḥ prātaḥ samutthāya prātaḥ kṛtyaṃ samāpya ca /
tilahomānvyāhṛtibhiḥ sahasraṃra kāvyeddvijaiḥ //
1.17.d:
ततः प्रातः समुत्थाय प्रातः कृत्यं समाप्य च ।
तिलहोमान्व्याहृतिभिः सहस्रंर काव्येद्द्विजैः ॥
1.17.m: Then, having risen at dawn and finished one's morning duties, / one should have Brahmins perform a thousand fire oblations of sesame seeds with the sacred utterances.

1.17.s:
tataḥ saṃpūjayeddevaṃ gandhapuṣpādibhiḥ kramāt /
devasya purataḥ kuryātpurāṇaśravaṇaṃ tataḥ //
1.17.d:
ततः संपूजयेद्देवं गन्धपुष्पादिभिः क्रमात् ।
देवस्य पुरतः कुर्यात्पुराणश्रवणं ततः ॥
1.17.m: Then one should worship the God in due order with scents, flowers, and the like; / then one should listen to the Purāṇas before the God.

1.17.s:
dadyāddvādaśaviprebhyo dadhyannaṃ pāyasaṃ pāyasaṃ tathā /
apūpairdaśa bhiryuktaṃ saghṛtaṃ ca sadakṣiṇam //
1.17.d:
दद्याद्द्वादशविप्रेभ्यो दध्यन्नं पायसं पायसं तथा ।
अपूपैर्दश भिर्युक्तं सघृतं च सदक्षिणम् ॥
1.17.m: One should give to twelve Brahmins curd-rice and sweet milk-rice, / along with ten sweet cakes, accompanied with clarified butter and priestly gifts.

1.17.s:
devadevajagannātha bhaktānugrahavigraha /
gṛhāṇopāyanaṃ kṛṣṇa sarvābhīṣṭaprado bhava //
1.17.d:
देवदेवजगन्नाथ भक्तानुग्रहविग्रह ।
गृहाणोपायनं कृष्ण सर्वाभीष्टप्रदो भव ॥
1.17.m: “O God of gods, Lord of the world, whose form is compassion to devotees! / Accept this offering, O Kṛṣṇa, and be the bestower of all desired wishes.”

1.17.s:
anenopāyanaṃ dattvā prārthaye māñjaliḥ sthitaḥ /
ādhāya jānunī bhūmau vinayāvananato vratī //
1.17.d:
अनेनोपायनं दत्त्वा प्रार्थये माञ्जलिः स्थितः ।
आधाय जानुनी भूमौ विनयावननतो व्रती ॥
1.17.m: Having presented the offering with this [mantra], the practitioner of the vow, / placing both knees upon the earth and bowing down in humility, should pray with cupped hands:

1.17.s:
namo namaste surarājarāja namo 'stute devaṃ jagannivāsa /
kuruṣva saṃpṛrṇaphalaṃ mamādya namo 'stu tubhyaṃ puruṣottamāya //
1.17.d:
नमो नमस्ते सुरराजराज नमो ऽस्तुते देवं जगन्निवास ।
कुरुष्व संपृर्णफलं ममाद्य नमो ऽस्तु तुभ्यं पुरुषोत्तमाय ॥
1.17.m: “Salutations, salutations to you, O King of the kings of gods! Salutations to you, O God, abode of the world! / Make my fruit complete today! Salutations to you, the Supreme Person!”

1.17.s:
iti saṃprārthayedviprāndevaṃ ca puruṣottamam /
dadyādarghyaṃ ca devāya mahālakṣmīyutāya vai //
1.17.d:
इति संप्रार्थयेद्विप्रान्देवं च पुरुषोत्तमम् ।
दद्यादर्घ्यं च देवाय महालक्ष्मीयुताय वै ॥
1.17.m: Thus he should pray to the Brahmins and to the God, the Supreme Person; / and he should present an offering of water to the God accompanied by Mahālakṣmī:

1.17.s:
lakṣmīpate namastubhyaṃ kṣīrārṇavanivāsine /
arghyaṃ gṛhāṇa deveśa lakṣmyā ca sahitaḥ prakṣo //
1.17.d:
लक्ष्मीपते नमस्तुभ्यं क्षीरार्णवनिवासिने ।
अर्घ्यं गृहाण देवेश लक्ष्म्या च सहितः प्रक्षो ॥
1.17.m: “Salutations to you, O Lord of Lakṣmī, dweller in the Milk Ocean! / Accept this offering of water, O Lord of gods, together with Lakṣmī, O Lord!”

1.17.s:
yasya smṛtyā ca nāmoktyā tapoyajñakriyādiṣu /
nyūnaṃ saṃpūrṇatāṃ yāti sadyo vande tamacyutam //
1.17.d:
यस्य स्मृत्या च नामोक्त्या तपोयज्ञक्रियादिषु ।
न्यूनं संपूर्णतां याति सद्यो वन्दे तमच्युतम् ॥
1.17.m: “Through the remembrance and recitation of whose name whatever is deficient / in austerities, sacrifices, rituals, and the like instantly reaches completeness—to that Acyuta I bow.”

1.17.s:
iti vijñāpya deveśaṃ tatsarvaṃ saṃyamī vrate /
pratimāṃ dakṣiṇāyuktāmācāryāya nivedayet //
1.17.d:
इति विज्ञाप्य देवेशं तत्सर्वं संयमी व्रते ।
प्रतिमां दक्षिणायुक्तामाचार्याय निवेदयेत् ॥
1.17.m: Having thus addressed the Lord of gods, the self-restrained observer of the vow / should offer all of that, [including] the idol accompanied with a priestly gift, to the teacher.

1.17.s:
brāhmaṇānbhojayetpaścīcchaktyā dadyāja dakṣiṇām /
bhuñjīta vāgyataḥ paścātsvayaṃ bevṛjanairvṛtaḥ //
1.17.d:
ब्राह्मणान्भोजयेत्पश्चीच्छक्त्या दद्याज दक्षिणाम् ।
भुञ्जीत वाग्यतः पश्चात्स्वयं बेवृजनैर्वृतः ॥
1.17.m: Afterwards he should feed Brahmins and give priestly gifts according to his means. / Afterwards, keeping silent, he should eat himself, surrounded by his kinsmen.

1.17.s:
āsāyaṃ śṛduyādviṣṇoḥ kathāṃ vidvajjanaiḥ saha /
ityevaṃ kurute yastu manujo dvādaśīvratam //
1.17.d:
आसायं शृदुयाद्विष्णोः कथां विद्वज्जनैः सह ।
इत्येवं कुरुते यस्तु मनुजो द्वादशीव्रतम् ॥
1.17.m: Until evening he should listen to the stories of Viṣṇu along with learned people. / That mortal who thus performs the observance of the twelfth day

1.17.s:
sarvānkāmānsa ānpoti paraghatreha ca nārada /
trisatakulasaṃyuktaḥ sarvapāpavivarjitaḥ /
tapāti viṣṇubhavanaṃ yatra yattvā na śocati //
1.17.d:
सर्वान्कामान्स आन्पोति परघत्रेह च नारद ।
त्रिसतकुलसंयुक्तः सर्वपापविवर्जितः ।
तपाति विष्णुभवनं यत्र यत्त्वा न शोचति ॥
1.17.m: attains all desires in this world and the next, O Nārada; / accompanied by three hundred generations of his family and freed from all sins, / he goes to the abode of Viṣṇu, having reached which he grieves no more.

1.17.s:
ya idaṃ śṛṇuyādvipra dvādaśīvratamuttamam /
vācayedvāpi sa naro vājapeyaphalaṃ labhet //
iti śrībṛhannāradīyapurāṇe pūrvabhāge prathamapāde vratākhyāne mārgaśīrṣaśukladvādaśīvratakathanaṃ nāma satpadaśo 'dhyāyaḥ
1.17.d:
य इदं शृणुयाद्विप्र द्वादशीव्रतमुत्तमम् ।
वाचयेद्वापि स नरो वाजपेयफलं लभेत् ॥
इति श्रीबृहन्नारदीयपुराणे पूर्वभागे प्रथमपादे व्रताख्याने मार्गशीर्षशुक्लद्वादशीव्रतकथनं नाम सत्पदशो ऽध्यायः
1.17.m:
Whoever hears this supreme observance of the twelfth day, O Brahmin, / or recites it, that man obtains the fruit of the Vājapeya sacrifice.

Thus ends the seventeenth chapter, titled 'The Account of the Observance of the Bright Twelfth Day of Mārgaśīrṣa', in the narration of vows in the first quarter of the first part of the venerable Bṛhannāradīya Purāṇa.

1.18.s:
sanaka uvāca
anyadvratavaraṃ vakṣya śṛṇuṣva munisattama /
sarvapāpaharaṃ puṇyaṃ sarvaduḥkhanibarhaṇam //
1.18.d:
सनक उवाच
अन्यद्व्रतवरं वक्ष्य शृणुष्व मुनिसत्तम ।
सर्वपापहरं पुण्यं सर्वदुःखनिबर्हणम् ॥
1.18.m: Sanaka said: / I shall declare another excellent observance; listen, O best of sages, / which destroys all sins, is holy, and removes all sorrow,

1.18.s:
brāhmaṇakṣatriyaviśāṃ śūdrāṇāṃ yoṣitāṃ tathā /
samastakāmaphaladaṃ sarvavratamyaphalapradam //
1.18.d:
ब्राह्मणक्षत्रियविशां शूद्राणां योषितां तथा ।
समस्तकामफलदं सर्वव्रतम्यफलप्रदम् ॥
1.18.m: for Brahmins, Kṣatriyas, Vaiśyas, Śūdras, and women, / granting the fruit of all desires, yielding the fruit of all vows,

1.18.s:
duḥsvanpanāśane dharmyaṃ duṣṭagrahanivāraṇam /
sarvalokeṣu vikhyātaṃ pūrṇimāvratamam /
yena cīrṇena pāpānāṃ rāśikoṭiḥra praśāmyati //
1.18.d:
दुःस्वन्पनाशने धर्म्यं दुष्टग्रहनिवारणम् ।
सर्वलोकेषु विख्यातं पूर्णिमाव्रतमम् ।
येन चीर्णेन पापानां राशिकोटिःर प्रशाम्यति ॥
1.18.m: righteous, destroying bad dreams, averting malignant planets, / renowned in all the worlds: the observance of the full moon, / through the performance of which ten million masses of sins are pacified.

1.18.s:
mārgaśīrṣe sitepakṣe pūrṇāyāṃ niyataḥ śuciḥ /
snānaṃ kuryādyathācāraṃ dantadhāvanapūrvakam //
1.18.d:
मार्गशीर्षे सितेपक्षे पूर्णायां नियतः शुचिः ।
स्नानं कुर्याद्यथाचारं दन्तधावनपूर्वकम् ॥
1.18.m: In the month of Mārgaśīrṣa, on the bright full-moon day, self-controlled and pure, / one should bathe according to custom after cleaning one's teeth.

1.18.s:
śuklāmbaradharaḥ śuddho gṛhamāgagatya vāgyataḥ /
prakṣālya pādāvācamya smaratrārāyaṇaṃ prabhum //
1.18.d:
शुक्लाम्बरधरः शुद्धो गृहमागगत्य वाग्यतः ।
प्रक्षाल्य पादावाचम्य स्मरत्रारायणं प्रभुम् ॥
1.18.m: Wearing white garments, pure, having returned home, restrained in speech, / having washed one's feet and sipped water, remembering the Lord Nārāyaṇa,

1.18.s:
nityaṃ devārcanaṃ kṛtvā paśvātsaṃkalpapūrvakam /
lakṣmī nārāyaṇaṃ devamarcayedbhaktibhāvataḥ //
1.18.d:
नित्यं देवार्चनं कृत्वा पश्वात्संकल्पपूर्वकम् ।
लक्ष्मी नारायणं देवमर्चयेद्भक्तिभावतः ॥
1.18.m: having performed the daily worship of the deity, and then having made the ritual intention, / one should worship the God Lakṣmīnārāyaṇa with devoted feeling.

1.18.s:
āvāhanāsanādyaiśca gandhapuṣpādibhirvratī /
namo nārāyaṇāyeti pūjayedbhaktitatparaḥ //
1.18.d:
आवाहनासनाद्यैश्च गन्धपुष्पादिभिर्व्रती ।
नमो नारायणायेति पूजयेद्भक्तितत्परः ॥
1.18.m: With invocations, seats, and the like, and with scents, flowers, and other offerings, / intent on devotion, the practitioner of the vow should worship him, saying, “Salutations to Nārāyaṇa.”

1.18.s:
gītairvādyaiśca nṛtyaiśca purāṇapaṭhanādibhiḥ /
stotrairvārādhayeddevaṃ vratakṛtsusamāhitaḥ //
1.18.d:
गीतैर्वाद्यैश्च नृत्यैश्च पुराणपठनादिभिः ।
स्तोत्रैर्वाराधयेद्देवं व्रतकृत्सुसमाहितः ॥
1.18.m: With songs, musical instruments, dances, readings from the Purāṇas, and other acts, / and with hymns of praise, the practitioner of the vow, deeply concentrated, should propitiate the God.

1.18.s:
devasya purataḥ kṛtvā sthaṇḍilaṃ caturastrakam /
aratnimātraṃ tatrāngiṃ sthāpayedgṛhyamārgataḥ /
ājyabhāgāntarpayantaṃ kṛtvā puruṣasūktataḥ /
caraṇā ca tilaiśvāpi ghṛtena juhuyāttathā //
1.18.d:
देवस्य पुरतः कृत्वा स्थण्डिलं चतुरस्त्रकम् ।
अरत्निमात्रं तत्रान्गिं स्थापयेद्गृह्यमार्गतः ।
आज्यभागान्तर्पयन्तं कृत्वा पुरुषसूक्ततः ।
चरणा च तिलैश्वापि घृतेन जुहुयात्तथा ॥
1.18.m: Having made a four-cornered altar of one cubit in size before the God, / one should establish the fire there according to the domestic ritual rule; / having performed [the rites] up to the portions of clarified butter, according to the Puruṣasūkta / and with the sacrificial caru, sesame seeds, and clarified butter, one should offer fire oblations.

1.18.s:
ekavāraṃ dvivāraṃ vātrivāraṃ vāpi śaktitaḥ /
homaṃ kuryātprayatnena sarvapāpanivṛttaye //
1.18.d:
एकवारं द्विवारं वात्रिवारं वापि शक्तितः ।
होमं कुर्यात्प्रयत्नेन सर्वपापनिवृत्तये ॥
1.18.m: Once, twice, or thrice, according to one's capacity, / one should diligently perform the fire oblation for the cessation of all sins.

1.18.s:
prāyaścittā dikaṃ sarvaṃ svagṛhyoktavidhānataḥ /
samāpya homaṃ vidhivacchāntisūktaṃ japedrudhaḥ //
1.18.d:
प्रायश्चित्ता दिकं सर्वं स्वगृह्योक्तविधानतः ।
समाप्य होमं विधिवच्छान्तिसूक्तं जपेद्रुधः ॥
1.18.m: Having concluded all the rites such as expiations in accordance with the rule of one's own domestic manual / and finished the fire oblation properly, the wise man should recite the Śāntisūkta.

1.18.s:
paścāddevaṃ samāgatya punaḥ pūjāṃ prakalpayet /
tathopavāsaṃ devāya hyarpayedbhaktisaṃyutaḥ //
1.18.d:
पश्चाद्देवं समागत्य पुनः पूजां प्रकल्पयेत् ।
तथोपवासं देवाय ह्यर्पयेद्भक्तिसंयुतः ॥
1.18.m: Afterwards, approaching the God, he should arrange worship again; / and endowed with devotion, he should dedicate his fasting to the God:

1.18.s:
paurṇamāsyāṃ nirāhāraḥ sthitvā deva tavājñayā /
bhokṣyāmi puṇḍarīkākṣa pare 'hli śaraṇaṃ bhava //
1.18.d:
पौर्णमास्यां निराहारः स्थित्वा देव तवाज्ञया ।
भोक्ष्यामि पुण्डरीकाक्ष परे ऽह्लि शरणं भव ॥
1.18.m: “Remaining without food on the full-moon day, O God, by your command, / I shall eat on the following day, O Lotus-eyed One; be my refuge!”

1.18.s:
iti vijñāpya devāyahyarghyaṃ dadyāttathaindave /
jānubhyāmavanīṃ gagatvā śuklapuṣpākṣatānvitaḥ //
1.18.d:
इति विज्ञाप्य देवायह्यर्घ्यं दद्यात्तथैन्दवे ।
जानुभ्यामवनीं गगत्वा शुक्लपुष्पाक्षतान्वितः ॥
1.18.m: Having addressed the God thus, he should also offer water to the Moon; / going down on his knees to the ground, accompanied with white flowers and unbroken rice grains:

1.18.s:
kṣīrodārṇavasaṃbhūta aghatrigotrasamudbhaghava /
grahāṇārghyaṃ mayā dattaṃ rohiṇīnāyaka prabho /
evamarghyaṃ pradāyendoḥ prārthayetprāñjalistataḥ //
1.18.d:
क्षीरोदार्णवसंभूत अघत्रिगोत्रसमुद्भघव ।
ग्रहाणार्घ्यं मया दत्तं रोहिणीनायक प्रभो ।
एवमर्घ्यं प्रदायेन्दोः प्रार्थयेत्प्राञ्जलिस्ततः ॥
1.18.m: “O born from the Ocean of Milk! O born in the lineage of Atri! / Accept the offering of water given by me, O Lord, husband of Rohiṇī!” / Having thus given the offering of water to the Moon, he should then pray with cupped hands,

1.18.s: tiṣṭanpūrvamukho bhūtvā paśyanninduṃ ca nārada //
1.18.d: तिष्टन्पूर्वमुखो भूत्वा पश्यन्निन्दुं च नारद ॥
1.18.m: standing facing the east and looking at the Moon, O Nārada:

1.18.s:
namaḥ śuklāṃśave tubhyaṃ dvijarājāya te namaḥ /
rohiṇīpataye tubhyaṃ lakṣmībhrātre namo 'stu te //
1.18.d:
नमः शुक्लांशवे तुभ्यं द्विजराजाय ते नमः ।
रोहिणीपतये तुभ्यं लक्ष्मीभ्रात्रे नमो ऽस्तु ते ॥
1.18.m: “Salutations to you of white rays! Salutations to you, king of the stars! / Salutations to you, husband of Rohiṇī! Salutations be to you, brother of Lakṣmī!”

1.18.s:
tataśca jāgaraṃ kuryātpurāṇaśravaṇādibhiḥ /
jitendriyaśca saṃśuddhaḥ pāṣaṇḍālokavarjitaḥ //
1.18.d:
ततश्च जागरं कुर्यात्पुराणश्रवणादिभिः ।
जितेन्द्रियश्च संशुद्धः पाषण्डालोकवर्जितः ॥
1.18.m: And then he should keep vigil by listening to the Purāṇas and similar means, / with senses conquered, completely purified, and avoiding the sight of heretics.

1.18.s:
tataḥ prātaḥ prakurvīta svācāraṃ ca yathāvidhi /
punaḥ saṃpūjayeddevaṃ yathāvibhavavistaram //
1.18.d:
ततः प्रातः प्रकुर्वीत स्वाचारं च यथाविधि ।
पुनः संपूजयेद्देवं यथाविभवविस्तरम् ॥
1.18.m: Then at dawn he should perform his customary duties according to the rule, / and worship the God again according to the extent of his wealth.

1.18.s:
brāhmaṇānbhojayecchaktyā tataśca prayato naraḥ /
bandhubhṛtyādibhiḥ sārdhaṃ svayaṃ bhuñjīta vāgyataḥ //
1.18.d:
ब्राह्मणान्भोजयेच्छक्त्या ततश्च प्रयतो नरः ।
बन्धुभृत्यादिभिः सार्धं स्वयं भुञ्जीत वाग्यतः ॥
1.18.m: Then, according to his capacity, the self-controlled man should feed Brahmins; / together with his relatives, servants, and others, he should himself eat, keeping silent.

1.18.s:
evaṃ pauṣādimāseṣu pūrṇamāsyāmupoṣitaḥ /
arcayedbhaktisaṃyukto nārāyaṇamanāyamam //
1.18.d:
एवं पौषादिमासेषु पूर्णमास्यामुपोषितः ।
अर्चयेद्भक्तिसंयुक्तो नारायणमनायमम् ॥
1.18.m: Having fasted thus on the full-moon day in the months beginning with Pauṣa, / endowed with devotion he should worship the imperishable Nārāyaṇa.

1.18.s:
evaṃ saṃvatsaraṃ kṛtvā kārtikyāṃ pūrṇimādine /
udyāpanaṃ prakurvīta tadvidhānaṃ vadāmi te //
1.18.d:
एवं संवत्सरं कृत्वा कार्तिक्यां पूर्णिमादिने ।
उद्यापनं प्रकुर्वीत तद्विधानं वदामि ते ॥
1.18.m: Having done so for a year, on the full-moon day of Kārttika / he should perform the concluding rite. I will tell you the rule for it:

1.18.s:
maṇḍapaṃ kārayeddivyaṃ caturastraṃ sumaṅgalam /
śobhitaṃ puṣpamālābhirvitānadhvajarājitam //
1.18.d:
मण्डपं कारयेद्दिव्यं चतुरस्त्रं सुमङ्गलम् ।
शोभितं पुष्पमालाभिर्वितानध्वजराजितम् ॥
1.18.m: He should have a celestial pavilion constructed, four-cornered and highly auspicious, / adorned with garlands of flowers, splendid with canopies and banners,

1.18.s:
bahudāpasamākīrṇaṃ kiṅkiṇījālaśobhitam /
darpaṃṇaiścāmaraiścaiva kalaśaiśca samāvṛtam //
1.18.d:
बहुदापसमाकीर्णं किङ्किणीजालशोभितम् ।
दर्पंणैश्चामरैश्चैव कलशैश्च समावृतम् ॥
1.18.m: filled with many lamps, decorated with clusters of tiny bells, / and surrounded with mirrors, fly-whisks, and water jars.

1.18.s:
tanmadhye sarvatobhadraṃ pañcavarṇavirājitam /
jalapūrṇaṃ tataḥ kumbhaṃ nyasettasyopari dvija //
1.18.d:
तन्मध्ये सर्वतोभद्रं पञ्चवर्णविराजितम् ।
जलपूर्णं ततः कुम्भं न्यसेत्तस्योपरि द्विज ॥
1.18.m: In the middle of it, a sarvatobhadra diagram shining with five colors; / then, O Brahmin, upon it he should place a water jar filled with water.

1.18.s:
pidhāya kumbhaṃ vastreṇa susūkṣmeṇāti śobhitam /
henmā vā rajatenāpi tathā tānmeṇa vā dvija /
lakṣmīnārāyaṇaṃ devaṃ kṛtvā tasyopari nyaset //
1.18.d:
पिधाय कुम्भं वस्त्रेण सुसूक्ष्मेणाति शोभितम् ।
हेन्मा वा रजतेनापि तथा तान्मेण वा द्विज ।
लक्ष्मीनारायणं देवं कृत्वा तस्योपरि न्यसेत् ॥
1.18.m: Having covered the jar with a very fine and exceedingly beautiful cloth, / having fashioned the god Lakṣmīnārāyaṇa out of gold or silver or copper, O twice-born one, / one should place it upon it.

1.18.s:
pañcāmṛtena saṃsnāpyābhyarcyagandhādibhiḥ kramāt /
bhakṣmairbhojyādinaivedyairbhaktitaḥ saṃyatendriyaḥ //
1.18.d:
पञ्चामृतेन संस्नाप्याभ्यर्च्यगन्धादिभिः क्रमात् ।
भक्ष्मैर्भोज्यादिनैवेद्यैर्भक्तितः संयतेन्द्रियः ॥
1.18.m: Having bathed [the deity] with the five nectars and worshipped him in proper sequence with fragrant perfumes and other offerings, / with edible pastries, cooked dishes, and other food-offerings, with devotion and senses restrained,

1.18.s:
jāgaraṃ ca tathā kuryārtsamyakchraraddhāsamanvitaḥ /
pare 'hni prātarvidhiva tpūrvavadviṣṇumarcayet //
1.18.d:
जागरं च तथा कुर्यार्त्सम्यक्छ्ररद्धासमन्वितः ।
परे ऽह्नि प्रातर्विधिव त्पूर्ववद्विष्णुमर्चयेत् ॥
1.18.m: one should also hold a night-vigil endowed with complete faith. / The next day, in the morning, one should worship Viṣṇu according to rule as before.

1.18.s:
ācāryāya pradātavyā pratimā dakṣaghiṇānvitā /
brāhmaṇānbhojayecchaktyā vibhave satyavāritam //
1.18.d:
आचार्याय प्रदातव्या प्रतिमा दक्षघिणान्विता ।
ब्राह्मणान्भोजयेच्छक्त्या विभवे सत्यवारितम् ॥
1.18.m: The image, accompanied by a priestly gift, must be given to the preceptor. / One should feed brāhmaṇas according to one's capacity, unstintingly if wealth permits.

1.18.s:
tiladānaṃ prakurvīta yathāśaktyā samāhitaḥ /
kuryādrangau ca vidhivatilahomaṃ vicakṣiṇaḥ //
1.18.d:
तिलदानं प्रकुर्वीत यथाशक्त्या समाहितः ।
कुर्याद्रन्गौ च विधिवतिलहोमं विचक्षिणः ॥
1.18.m: Composed in mind, one should give a gift of sesame seeds according to one's ability. / In the sacrificial arena, the wise man should perform a fire oblation with sesame seeds according to rule.

1.18.s:
evaṃ kṛtvā naraḥ samyak lakṣmīnārāyaṇavratam /
iha bhuktvā mahābhogānputraghapautraghasamanvitaḥ //
1.18.d:
एवं कृत्वा नरः सम्यक् लक्ष्मीनारायणव्रतम् ।
इह भुक्त्वा महाभोगान्पुत्रघपौत्रघसमन्वितः ॥
1.18.m: A person having thus properly performed the observance of Lakṣmīnārāyaṇa, / enjoying great pleasures here [in this world] accompanied by sons and grandsons,

1.18.s:
sarvapāpavinirmuktaḥ kulāyutasamanvitaḥ /
prayāti viṣṇubhavanaṃ yogināmapi durlabham //
iti śrībṛhannāradīyapurāṇe pūrvabhāge prathamapāde vratākhyāne māgaśīrṣapaurṇimāyāṃ lakṣaghmīnārāyaṇavrataṃ nāmāṣṭādaśo 'dhyāyaḥ
1.18.d:
सर्वपापविनिर्मुक्तः कुलायुतसमन्वितः ।
प्रयाति विष्णुभवनं योगिनामपि दुर्लभम् ॥
इति श्रीबृहन्नारदीयपुराणे पूर्वभागे प्रथमपादे व्रताख्याने मागशीर्षपौर्णिमायां लक्षघ्मीनारायणव्रतं नामाष्टादशो ऽध्यायः
1.18.m:
freed from all sins and accompanied by ten thousand of his lineage, / goes to the abode of Viṣṇu, difficult to attain even for yogins.

Thus ends the eighteenth chapter, named The Observance of Lakṣmīnārāyaṇa on the Full Moon of Mārgaśīrṣa, in the narration of observances in the first quarter of the first part of the venerable Bṛhannāradīya Purāṇa.

1.19.s:
sanaka uvāca
anyadvūtaṃ pravakṣyāmi dhvajāropaṇasaṃjñitam /
sarvapāpaharaṃ puṇyaṃ viṣṇuprīṇanakāraṇam //
1.19.d:
सनक उवाच
अन्यद्वूतं प्रवक्ष्यामि ध्वजारोपणसंज्ञितम् ।
सर्वपापहरं पुण्यं विष्णुप्रीणनकारणम् ॥
1.19.m: Sanaka said: / I shall declare another observance, called the Erection of the Flag, / which removes all sins, yields merit, and causes the delight of Viṣṇu.

1.19.s:
yaḥ kuryādviṣṇubhavane dhvajāropaṇamuttamam /
saṃpūjyate vigniñcyādyaiḥ kimanyairbahubhāṣitaiḥ //
1.19.d:
यः कुर्याद्विष्णुभवने ध्वजारोपणमुत्तमम् ।
संपूज्यते विग्निञ्च्याद्यैः किमन्यैर्बहुभाषितैः ॥
1.19.m: Whoever performs the excellent erection of the flag in Viṣṇu's temple / is worshipped by Brahmā and the other gods; what need is there of saying much else?

1.19.s:
hemabhārasahasraṃ tu yo dadāti kuṭumbine /
tatphalaṃ tulyamātraṃ syāddhūjāropaṇakarmaṇaḥ //
1.19.d:
हेमभारसहस्रं तु यो ददाति कुटुम्बिने ।
तत्फलं तुल्यमात्रं स्याद्धूजारोपणकर्मणः ॥
1.19.m: He who gives a thousand measures of gold to a householder— / that fruit is merely equal to the rite of erecting the flag.

1.19.s:
dhvajāropaṇatulyaṃ syādgaṅgāsnānamanuttamam /
athavā tulasūsevā śivaliṅgaprapūjanam //
1.19.d:
ध्वजारोपणतुल्यं स्याद्गङ्गास्नानमनुत्तमम् ।
अथवा तुलसूसेवा शिवलिङ्गप्रपूजनम् ॥
1.19.m: Bathing in the Gaṅgā, than which nothing is higher, / or attendance upon tulasī, or the worship of the liṅga of Śiva, would equal the erection of the flag.

1.19.s:
aho 'pūrvamaho 'pūrvamaho 'pūrvamidaṃ dvija /
sarvapāpa haraṃ karma dhvajāgopaṇasaṃjñitam //
1.19.d:
अहो ऽपूर्वमहो ऽपूर्वमहो ऽपूर्वमिदं द्विज ।
सर्वपाप हरं कर्म ध्वजागोपणसंज्ञितम् ॥
1.19.m: Ah, wonderful! Ah, wonderful! Ah, wonderful is this rite, O twice-born one, / called the erection of the flag, which removes all sins!

1.19.s:
santi vai yāni kāryāṇi dhvajāropaṇakarmaṇi /
tāni sarvāṇi vakṣyāmi śṛṇuṣva gadato mama //
1.19.d:
सन्ति वै यानि कार्याणि ध्वजारोपणकर्मणि ।
तानि सर्वाणि वक्ष्यामि शृणुष्व गदतो मम ॥
1.19.m: Whatever duties there are in the rite of erecting the flag, / all of them I shall declare; listen to me speaking.

1.19.s:
kārtikasya site pakṣaghe daśamyāṃ prayato naraḥ /
snānaṃ kuryātprayatnena dantadhāvanapūrvakam //
1.19.d:
कार्तिकस्य सिते पक्षघे दशम्यां प्रयतो नरः ।
स्नानं कुर्यात्प्रयत्नेन दन्तधावनपूर्वकम् ॥
1.19.m: On the tenth day in the bright half of Kārtika, a restrained man / should diligently take a bath after first cleaning his teeth.

1.19.s:
ekāśī brahmacārī ca svapennārāyaṇaṃ smaran /
dhautāmbaradharaḥ śuddho vipro nārāyaṇāgrataḥ //
1.19.d:
एकाशी ब्रह्मचारी च स्वपेन्नारायणं स्मरन् ।
धौताम्बरधरः शुद्धो विप्रो नारायणाग्रतः ॥
1.19.m: Eating once a day and celibate, wearing washed clothes, / pure, the brāhmaṇa should sleep before Nārāyaṇa, remembering Nārāyaṇa.

1.19.s:
tataḥ prātaḥ samutthāya snātvācamya yathāvidhi /
nityakarmāṇi nirvartya paścādviṣṇuṃ samarcayet //
1.19.d:
ततः प्रातः समुत्थाय स्नात्वाचम्य यथाविधि ।
नित्यकर्माणि निर्वर्त्य पश्चाद्विष्णुं समर्चयेत् ॥
1.19.m: Then, having risen in the morning, bathed, and sipped water according to rule, / and having performed the daily duties, he should thereafter worship Viṣṇu.

1.19.s:
caturbhirbrāhmaṇaiḥ sārdhdaṃ kṛtvā ca svastivācanam /
nāndīśrāddhaṃ prakurvīta dhvajāropaṇakarmaṇi //
1.19.d:
चतुर्भिर्ब्राह्मणैः सार्ध्दं कृत्वा च स्वस्तिवाचनम् ।
नान्दीश्राद्धं प्रकुर्वीत ध्वजारोपणकर्मणि ॥
1.19.m: Having performed the recitation of auspicious blessings together with four brāhmaṇas, / he should perform the nāndīśrāddha in the rite of erecting the flag.

1.19.s:
dhvajastambho ca gāyatryā prokṣaghayedvastrasaṃyutau /
sūryaṃ ca vainateyaṃ ca himāṃśuṃ tatparor'cayet //
1.19.d:
ध्वजस्तम्भो च गायत्र्या प्रोक्षघयेद्वस्त्रसंयुतौ ।
सूर्यं च वैनतेयं च हिमांशुं तत्परोर्ऽचयेत् ॥
1.19.m: He should sprinkle the two flagstaffs, draped with cloth, with the gāyatrī, / and thereafter worship the Sun, Garuḍa, and the Moon.

1.19.s:
dhātāraṃ ca vidhātāraṃ pūjayeddhajadaṇḍake /
haridrākṣaghatagandhādyaiḥ śuklapuṣpairviśeṣataḥ //
1.19.d:
धातारं च विधातारं पूजयेद्धजदण्डके ।
हरिद्राक्षघतगन्धाद्यैः शुक्लपुष्पैर्विशेषतः ॥
1.19.m: And on the flagstaff he should worship Dhātṛ and Vidhātṛ / with turmeric, unbroken rice, fragrant perfumes, and other offerings, especially with white flowers.

1.19.s:
tato gocarmamātraghaṃ tu sthaṇḍilaṃ copalipya vai /
ādhāyāngiṃ svagṛhyottyā hyājyabhāgādikaṃ kramāt //
1.19.d:
ततो गोचर्ममात्रघं तु स्थण्डिलं चोपलिप्य वै ।
आधायान्गिं स्वगृह्योत्त्या ह्याज्यभागादिकं क्रमात् ॥
1.19.m: Then, having smeared a sacrificial ground measuring a cow-hide, / having established the fire according to the precepts of his own domestic ritual manual, [and offered] the portions of clarified butter and so forth in order,

1.19.s:
juhuyātpāyasaṃ caiva sājyamaṣṭottaraṃ śatam /
prathamaṃ pauruṣaṃ sūktaṃ viṣṇornukamirāvatīm //
1.19.d:
जुहुयात्पायसं चैव साज्यमष्टोत्तरं शतम् ।
प्रथमं पौरुषं सूक्तं विष्णोर्नुकमिरावतीम् ॥
1.19.m: he should offer one hundred and eight oblations of milk-rice mixed with clarified butter, / first reciting the Puruṣasūkta, then 'viṣṇor nu kam', and the Irāvatī [hymn].

1.19.s:
tataśca vainateyāya svāhe tyaṣṭāhutīstathā /
somo dhenumudutyaṃ ca juhuyācca tato dvija //
1.19.d:
ततश्च वैनतेयाय स्वाहे त्यष्टाहुतीस्तथा ।
सोमो धेनुमुदुत्यं च जुहुयाच्च ततो द्विज ॥
1.19.m: Then, uttering 'svāhā to the son of Vinatā', he should likewise offer eight oblations, / and then, O twice-born one, offer with 'somo dhenum' and 'ud u tyam'.

1.19.s:
sauramantrāñjapettaghatra śāntisūtkāni śaktitaḥ /
rātraghau jāgaraṇaṃ kuryādupakaṇṭhaṃ hareḥ śucuḥ //
1.19.d:
सौरमन्त्राञ्जपेत्तघत्र शान्तिसूत्कानि शक्तितः ।
रात्रघौ जागरणं कुर्यादुपकण्ठं हरेः शुचुः ॥
1.19.m: He should recite the solar mantras there and the hymns of pacification according to his capacity; / pure, he should keep a night-vigil near Hari.

1.19.s:
tataḥ prātaḥ samutthāya nityakarma samāpya ca /
gandhapuṣpādibhirdevamarcayetpūrvavatkramāt //
1.19.d:
ततः प्रातः समुत्थाय नित्यकर्म समाप्य च ।
गन्धपुष्पादिभिर्देवमर्चयेत्पूर्ववत्क्रमात् ॥
1.19.m: Then, having risen in the morning and completed his daily duties, / he should worship the god in order with fragrant perfumes, flowers, and other offerings as before.

1.19.s:
tato maṅgalavādyaiśca sūktapāṭhaiśca śaubhanam /
nṛtyaiśca ratotraghapaṭhanairnayedviṣṇavālaye dhvajam //
1.19.d:
ततो मङ्गलवाद्यैश्च सूक्तपाठैश्च शौभनम् ।
नृत्यैश्च रतोत्रघपठनैर्नयेद्विष्णवालये ध्वजम् ॥
1.19.m: Then, with auspicious musical instruments, recitations of Vedic hymns, / dances, and recitations of hymns of praise, he should carry the splendid flag to Viṣṇu's temple.

1.19.s:
devasya dvāradeśe vā śikhare vā mudānvitaḥ /
susthuraḥ sthāpayedvipra dhvajaṃ sastambhasaṃyutam //
1.19.d:
देवस्य द्वारदेशे वा शिखरे वा मुदान्वितः ।
सुस्थुरः स्थापयेद्विप्र ध्वजं सस्तम्भसंयुतम् ॥
1.19.m: Filled with joy, O brāhmaṇa, he should firmly erect / the flag together with its staff, either at the temple's gateway or on its pinnacle.

1.19.s:
gandhapuṣpāghakṣatairddevaṃ dhūpadīparmanoharaiḥ /
bhakṣaghyabhojyādisaṃyuktairnaivedyaiśca hariṃ yajet //
1.19.d:
गन्धपुष्पाघक्षतैर्द्देवं धूपदीपर्मनोहरैः ।
भक्षघ्यभोज्यादिसंयुक्तैर्नैवेद्यैश्च हरिं यजेत् ॥
1.19.m: He should worship the god Hari with fragrant perfumes, flowers, unbroken rice, captivating incense and lamps, / and with food-offerings consisting of edible pastries, cooked dishes, and the like.

1.19.s:
evaṃ devālaye sthāpya śobhanaṃ dhvajamuttamam /
pradakṣaghiṇamanuvrajya stotraghametadudūrayet //
1.19.d:
एवं देवालये स्थाप्य शोभनं ध्वजमुत्तमम् ।
प्रदक्षघिणमनुव्रज्य स्तोत्रघमेतदुदूरयेत् ॥
1.19.m: Having thus erected the auspicious and excellent flag in the god's abode, / and having walked circumambulating it, he should utter this hymn of praise:

1.19.s:
namaste puṇḍarīkākṣa namaste viśvabhāvana /
namaste 'stu hṛṣīkeśa mahāpuruṣa pūrvaja //
1.19.d:
नमस्ते पुण्डरीकाक्ष नमस्ते विश्वभावन ।
नमस्ते ऽस्तु हृषीकेश महापुरुष पूर्वज ॥
1.19.m: "Homage to you, lotus-eyed one! Homage to you, creator of the universe! / Homage be to you, Hṛṣīkeśa, supreme Puruṣa, the first-born!

1.19.s:
yenedamakhilaṃ jātaṃ yatra sarvaṃ pratiṣṭitam /
layameṣyati yatraivaṃ taṃ prapanno 'smi keśavam //
1.19.d:
येनेदमखिलं जातं यत्र सर्वं प्रतिष्टितम् ।
लयमेष्यति यत्रैवं तं प्रपन्नो ऽस्मि केशवम् ॥
1.19.m: To him by whom this whole [universe] was born, in whom everything is established, / and into whom it shall dissolve—to that Keśava I have surrendered.

1.19.s:
na jānanti paraṃ bhāvaṃ yasya brahmādayaḥ surāḥ /
yoginoyaṃ na paśyanti taṃ vandaṃ jñānarupuṇam //
1.19.d:
न जानन्ति परं भावं यस्य ब्रह्मादयः सुराः ।
योगिनोयं न पश्यन्ति तं वन्दं ज्ञानरुपुणम् ॥
1.19.m: Whose highest nature Brahmā and the other gods do not know, / whom yogins do not behold—to him whose form is knowledge, I bow.

1.19.s:
antarikṣantu yannābhirdyairmūrddhā yasya caiva hi /
pādo 'bhūdyasya pṛthivī taṃ vande viśvarupiṇam //
1.19.d:
अन्तरिक्षन्तु यन्नाभिर्द्यैर्मूर्द्धा यस्य चैव हि ।
पादो ऽभूद्यस्य पृथिवी तं वन्दे विश्वरुपिणम् ॥
1.19.m: Whose navel is the intermediate space, whose head is heaven itself, / whose feet became the earth—to him whose form is the universe, I bow.

1.19.s:
yasya śrotre diśaḥ sarvā yaccakṣurdinakṛcajchaśī /
ṛksāmayajupī yena taṃ vande brahrarupiṇam //
1.19.d:
यस्य श्रोत्रे दिशः सर्वा यच्चक्षुर्दिनकृचज्छशी ।
ऋक्सामयजुपी येन तं वन्दे ब्रह्ररुपिणम् ॥
1.19.m: Whose ears are all the directions, whose eyes are the sun and the moon, / by whom exist the Ṛg, Sāman, and Yajur [Vedas]—to him whose form is Brahman, I bow.

1.19.s:
yanmukhādvāhmaṇā jātā yadvāhorabhavannṛpāḥ /
vaiśyā yasyo ruto jātāḥ padbhaghyāṃ śūdro vyajāyata //
1.19.d:
यन्मुखाद्वाह्मणा जाता यद्वाहोरभवन्नृपाः ।
वैश्या यस्यो रुतो जाताः पद्भघ्यां शूद्रो व्यजायत ॥
1.19.m: From whose mouth brāhmaṇas were born, from whose arms were kings, / the vaiśyas were born from his thighs, and from his feet the śūdra was born.

1.19.s:
māyāsaṅgamamātragheṇa vadanti puruṣaṃ tvajam /
svabhāvavimalaṃ śuddhaṃ nirvikāraṃ nirañjanam //
1.19.d:
मायासङ्गममात्रघेण वदन्ति पुरुषं त्वजम् ।
स्वभावविमलं शुद्धं निर्विकारं निरञ्जनम् ॥
1.19.m: They speak of the unborn Puruṣa merely through his contact with māyā, / who is by nature stainless, pure, changeless, and immaculate.

1.19.s:
kṣīrabdhi śāyinaṃ devamanantamaparājitam /
sadbhaktavatsalaṃ viṣṇuṃ bhaktigamyaṃ namāmyaham //
1.19.d:
क्षीरब्धि शायिनं देवमनन्तमपराजितम् ।
सद्भक्तवत्सलं विष्णुं भक्तिगम्यं नमाम्यहम् ॥
1.19.m: The god who reclines on the milk ocean, the infinite, unconquered, / affectionate toward true devotees, attainable through devotion—to Viṣṇu I bow.

1.19.s:
pṛthivyādīni bhūtāni tanmātrāṇīṃndriyāṇi ca /
sūkṣmāsūkṣyāṇi yenāsaṃstaṃ vande sarvatomukham //
1.19.d:
पृथिव्यादीनि भूतानि तन्मात्राणींन्द्रियाणि च ।
सूक्ष्मासूक्ष्याणि येनासंस्तं वन्दे सर्वतोमुखम् ॥
1.19.m: By whom the elements beginning with earth, the subtle elements, and the sense-organs, / both subtle and gross, came into being—to that all-facing one I bow.

1.19.s:
yadvahya paramaṃ dhāma sarvalokottamottamam /
nirguṇaṃ paramaṃ sūkṣmaṃ praṇato 'sti punaḥ punaḥ //
1.19.d:
यद्वह्य परमं धाम सर्वलोकोत्तमोत्तमम् ।
निर्गुणं परमं सूक्ष्मं प्रणतो ऽस्ति पुनः पुनः ॥
1.19.m: To that supreme abode of his, highest of all worlds, / devoid of qualities, transcendent, and subtle, I bow down again and again.

1.19.s:
avikāramajaṃ śuddhaṃ sarvatobāhumīśvaram /.
yamāmananti yogāndrāḥ sarvakāraṇakāraṇam //
1.19.d:
अविकारमजं शुद्धं सर्वतोबाहुमीश्वरम् ॥
यमामनन्ति योगान्द्राः सर्वकारणकारणम् ॥
1.19.m: The changeless, unborn, pure, lord with arms on all sides, / whom the lords of yoga declare to be the cause of all causes.

1.19.s:
yo devaḥ sarvabhūtānāmantarātmā jaganmayaḥ /
nirguṇaḥ paramātmā ca sa me viṣṇuḥ prasīdatu //
1.19.d:
यो देवः सर्वभूतानामन्तरात्मा जगन्मयः ।
निर्गुणः परमात्मा च स मे विष्णुः प्रसीदतु ॥
1.19.m: The god who is the inner self of all beings, composed of the universe, / devoid of qualities and the supreme self—may that Viṣṇu be pleased with me!

1.19.s:
hṛdayastho 'pi dūrastho māyayā mohitātmanām /
jñānināṃ sarvago yastu sa me viṣṇuḥ prasīdatu //
1.19.d:
हृदयस्थो ऽपि दूरस्थो मायया मोहितात्मनाम् ।
ज्ञानिनां सर्वगो यस्तु स मे विष्णुः प्रसीदतु ॥
1.19.m: Though residing in the heart, he is far away to those whose minds are deluded by māyā, / but omnipresent to the wise—may that Viṣṇu be pleased with me!

1.19.s:
caturbhiśca caturbhiśca dvābhyāṃ pañcabhireva ca /
hūyate ca punardvātārthaṃbhyāṃ sa me viṣṇuḥ pratīdatu //
1.19.d:
चतुर्भिश्च चतुर्भिश्च द्वाभ्यां पञ्चभिरेव च ।
हूयते च पुनर्द्वातार्थंभ्यां स मे विष्णुः प्रतीदतु ॥
1.19.m: He to whom offerings are made with four, with four, with two, with five, / and again with two [syllables]—may that Viṣṇu be pleased with me!

1.19.s:
jñānināṃ karmiṇāṃ caiva tathā bhaktimatāṃ nṛṇām /
gatidātā viśvamṛgyaḥ sa me viṣṇuḥ prasūdatu //
1.19.d:
ज्ञानिनां कर्मिणां चैव तथा भक्तिमतां नृणाम् ।
गतिदाता विश्वमृग्यः स मे विष्णुः प्रसूदतु ॥
1.19.m: The giver of the goal to men of knowledge, men of action, / and those endowed with devotion, sought by the whole universe—may that Viṣṇu be pleased with me!

1.19.s:
jagaddhitārthaṃ ye dehā dhriyante līlayā hareḥ /
tānarcayanti vibudhāḥ sa me viṣṇuḥ prasīdatu //
1.19.d:
जगद्धितार्थं ये देहा ध्रियन्ते लीलया हरेः ।
तानर्चयन्ति विबुधाः स मे विष्णुः प्रसीदतु ॥
1.19.m: The bodies assumed in sport by Hari for the welfare of the world, / which the wise revere—may that Viṣṇu be pleased with me!"

1.19.s:
yamāmanantive santaḥ saccidānandavigraham /
nirguṇaṃ ca guṇādhāraṃ sa me viṣṇuḥ prasīdatu //
1.19.d:
यमामनन्तिवे सन्तः सच्चिदानन्दविग्रहम् ।
निर्गुणं च गुणाधारं स मे विष्णुः प्रसीदतु ॥
1.19.m: Whom the virtuous declare to be the embodiment of existence, consciousness, and bliss, / devoid of qualities yet the support of all qualities—may that Viṣṇu be pleased with me.

1.19.s:
iti stutvā namedviṣṇuṃ brāhmaṇāṃśca prapūjayet /
ācāryaṃ pūjayetpaścāddakṣiṇācchādanādibhiḥ //
1.19.d:
इति स्तुत्वा नमेद्विष्णुं ब्राह्मणांश्च प्रपूजयेत् ।
आचार्यं पूजयेत्पश्चाद्दक्षिणाच्छादनादिभिः ॥
1.19.m: Having thus praised him, he should bow to Viṣṇu and worship the brahmins; / then he should worship the teacher with gifts of honorarium, garments, and the like.

1.19.s:
brāhmaṇānbhojayecchaktyā bhakti bhāvasamanvitaḥ /
putramatrikalatrādyaiḥ svayaṃ ca saha bandhubhiḥ //
1.19.d:
ब्राह्मणान्भोजयेच्छक्त्या भक्ति भावसमन्वितः ।
पुत्रमत्रिकलत्राद्यैः स्वयं च सह बन्धुभिः ॥
1.19.m: Endowed with a disposition of devotion, he should feed the brahmins according to his means, / and himself, along with his sons, friends, wife, and kinsmen,

1.19.s:
kurvīta pāraṇaṃ vipra nārāyaṇaparāyaṇaḥ /
yastvetatkarma kurvīta dhvajāropaṇamuttamam /
tasya puṇyaphalaṃ vakṣye śṛṇuṣva susamāhitaḥ //
1.19.d:
कुर्वीत पारणं विप्र नारायणपरायणः ।
यस्त्वेतत्कर्म कुर्वीत ध्वजारोपणमुत्तमम् ।
तस्य पुण्यफलं वक्ष्ये शृणुष्व सुसमाहितः ॥
1.19.m: devoted to Nārāyaṇa, should break his fast, O brahmin. / Whoever performs this supreme act of hoisting a flag, / I shall proclaim the fruit of his merit; listen with an attentive mind.

1.19.s:
paṭo dhvajasya viprendra yāvaccalati vāyunā /
tāvanti pāpajālāni naśyantyeva na saṃśayaḥ //
1.19.d:
पटो ध्वजस्य विप्रेन्द्र यावच्चलति वायुना ।
तावन्ति पापजालानि नश्यन्त्येव न संशयः ॥
1.19.m: As long as the cloth of the flag flutters in the wind, O foremost of brahmins, / so long do whole webs of sins perish; of this there is no doubt.

1.19.s:
mahāpātakayukto vā yukto vā sarvapātakaiḥ /
dhvajaṃ viṣṇugṛhe kṛtvā mucyate sarvapātakaiḥ //
1.19.d:
महापातकयुक्तो वा युक्तो वा सर्वपातकैः ।
ध्वजं विष्णुगृहे कृत्वा मुच्यते सर्वपातकैः ॥
1.19.m: Whether burdened with mortal sins or laden with all manner of sins, / by setting up a flag in Viṣṇu’s temple, one is liberated from all sins.

1.19.s:
yāvaddināni tiṣṭeta dhvajo viṣṇugṛhe dvija /
tāvadyugasahasrāṇi harisārupyamaśnute //
1.19.d:
यावद्दिनानि तिष्टेत ध्वजो विष्णुगृहे द्विज ।
तावद्युगसहस्राणि हरिसारुप्यमश्नुते ॥
1.19.m: For as many days as the flag remains in Viṣṇu’s temple, O twice-born one, / for that many thousands of yugas he attains conformity of form with Hari.

1.19.s:
āropitaṃ dhvajaṃ dṛṣṭvā ye 'bhinandanti dhārmikāḥ /
te 'pi sarve pramucyante mahāpātakakoṭibhiḥ //
1.19.d:
आरोपितं ध्वजं दृष्ट्वा ये ऽभिनन्दन्ति धार्मिकाः ।
ते ऽपि सर्वे प्रमुच्यन्ते महापातककोटिभिः ॥
1.19.m: Those righteous people who, seeing a hoisted flag, rejoice in it, / they too are all delivered from crores of mortal sins.

1.19.s:
āropito dhvajo viṣṇugṛhe dhunvanpaṭaṃ svakam /
kartuḥ sarvāṇi pāpāni dhunoti nimiṣārddhataḥ //
1.19.d:
आरोपितो ध्वजो विष्णुगृहे धुन्वन्पटं स्वकम् ।
कर्तुः सर्वाणि पापानि धुनोति निमिषार्द्धतः ॥
1.19.m: A flag hoisted in Viṣṇu’s temple, as it waves its cloth, / dispels all the performer's sins within half a twinkling of an eye.

1.19.s:
yastvā ropya gṛhe viṣṇordhvajaṃ nityamupācaret /
sa devayānena divaṃ yātīva sumatirnṛpaḥ //
iti śrībṛhannāradīyapurāṇe pūrvabhāge prathamapāde vratākhyāne dhvajāropaṇannāmaikonaviṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ
1.19.d:
यस्त्वा रोप्य गृहे विष्णोर्ध्वजं नित्यमुपाचरेत् ।
स देवयानेन दिवं यातीव सुमतिर्नृपः ॥
इति श्रीबृहन्नारदीयपुराणे पूर्वभागे प्रथमपादे व्रताख्याने ध्वजारोपणन्नामैकोनविंशो ऽध्यायः
1.19.m:
Whoever, having hoisted a flag in Viṣṇu’s house, tends to it constantly, / goes to heaven by the path of the gods, like the wise King Sumati.

Thus ends the nineteenth chapter, named 'The Hoisting of the Flag', in the discourse on observances in the first quarter of the first part of the venerable Bṛhannāradīya Purāṇa.

1.20.s:
nārada uvāca
bhagavansarvadharmajña sarvaśāstrārthapāraga /
sarvakarmavariṣṭaṃ ca tvayoktaṃ dhvajadhāraṇam //
1.20.d:
नारद उवाच
भगवन्सर्वधर्मज्ञ सर्वशास्त्रार्थपारग ।
सर्वकर्मवरिष्टं च त्वयोक्तं ध्वजधारणम् ॥
1.20.m: Nārada said: / O Lord, knower of all righteousness, conversant with the meaning of all scriptures, / the raising of a flag has been declared by you to be the foremost among all religious acts.

1.20.s:
yastu vai sumatirnāma dhvajāropaparo mune /
tvayoktastasya caritaṃ vistareṇa mamādiśa //
1.20.d:
यस्तु वै सुमतिर्नाम ध्वजारोपपरो मुने ।
त्वयोक्तस्तस्य चरितं विस्तरेण ममादिश ॥
1.20.m: He who was named Sumati, devoted to hoisting the flag, O sage, / and was mentioned by you—explain his story to me in full.

1.20.s:
sanaka uvāca
śṛṇuṣvaikamanāḥ puṇyamitihāsaṃ purātanamam /
brahmaṇā kathitaṃ mahyaṃ sarvapāpapraṇāśanam //
1.20.d:
सनक उवाच
शृणुष्वैकमनाः पुण्यमितिहासं पुरातनमम् ।
ब्रह्मणा कथितं मह्यं सर्वपापप्रणाशनम् ॥
1.20.m: Sanaka said: / Listen with single-minded focus to this ancient, sacred history / told to me by Brahmā, which destroys all sins.

1.20.s:
āsītpurā kṛtayuge sumatirnāma bhūpatiḥ /
somavaṃśodbhavaḥ śrīmānsatpadvīpaikanāyakaḥ //
1.20.d:
आसीत्पुरा कृतयुगे सुमतिर्नाम भूपतिः ।
सोमवंशोद्भवः श्रीमान्सत्पद्वीपैकनायकः ॥
1.20.m: In ancient times, in the Kṛta Yuga, there was a king named Sumati, / born of the Lunar dynasty, illustrious, the sole ruler of the seven continents,

1.20.s:
dharmātmā satyasaṃpannaḥ śucivaṃśyo 'tithipriyaḥ /
sarvalakṣaṇasaṃpannaḥ sarvasaṃpadvibhūṣitaḥ //
1.20.d:
धर्मात्मा सत्यसंपन्नः शुचिवंश्यो ऽतिथिप्रियः ।
सर्वलक्षणसंपन्नः सर्वसंपद्विभूषितः ॥
1.20.m: righteous-souled, endowed with truth, of pure lineage, fond of guests, / endowed with all auspicious marks, and adorned with all forms of prosperity,

1.20.s:
sadā harikathāsevī haripūjāparāyaṇaḥ /
haribhaktiparāṇāṃ ca śuśrūṣurnirahṝṅkṛtiḥ //
1.20.d:
सदा हरिकथासेवी हरिपूजापरायणः ।
हरिभक्तिपराणां च शुश्रूषुर्निरहॄङ्कृतिः ॥
1.20.m: always devoted to hearing stories of Hari, intent on worshipping Hari, / wishing to serve those devoted to Hari, free from egoism,

1.20.s:
pūjyapūjārato nityaṃ samadarśī guṇānvitaḥ /
sarvabhūtahitaḥ śāntaḥ kṛtajñaḥ kīrtimāṃstathā //
1.20.d:
पूज्यपूजारतो नित्यं समदर्शी गुणान्वितः ।
सर्वभूतहितः शान्तः कृतज्ञः कीर्तिमांस्तथा ॥
1.20.m: constantly engaged in worshipping the venerable, seeing all with an equal eye, endowed with virtues, / benevolent to all beings, tranquil, grateful, and renowned.

1.20.s:
tasya bhāryā mahābhāgā sarvalakṣaṇasaṃyutā /
pativratā patiprāṇā nāmrā satyamatirmune //
1.20.d:
तस्य भार्या महाभागा सर्वलक्षणसंयुता ।
पतिव्रता पतिप्राणा नाम्रा सत्यमतिर्मुने ॥
1.20.m: His wife, O sage, was highly fortunate, endowed with all auspicious marks, / devoted to her husband, holding her husband as her very breath, named Satyamatī.

1.20.s:
tādubhau dampatū nityaṃ haripūjāparāyaṇau /
jātismarau mahābhāgau satyajñau satparāyaṇau //
1.20.d:
तादुभौ दम्पतू नित्यं हरिपूजापरायणौ ।
जातिस्मरौ महाभागौ सत्यज्ञौ सत्परायणौ ॥
1.20.m: Both husband and wife were constantly intent on the worship of Hari; / highly fortunate, possessing memory of previous births, knowers of truth, dedicated to the good.

1.20.s:
annadānaratau nityaṃ jaladānaparāyaṇau /
taḍāgārāmavaprādau nasaṃkhyātānvitenatuḥ //
1.20.d:
अन्नदानरतौ नित्यं जलदानपरायणौ ।
तडागारामवप्रादौ नसंख्यातान्वितेनतुः ॥
1.20.m: Always devoted to giving food, intent on providing water, / they laid out countless tanks, gardens, ramparts, and the like.

1.20.s:
sā tu satyamatirnityaṃ śucirviṣṇugṛhe satī /
nṛtyatyatyantasantuṣṭā manojñā sañjuvādinī //
1.20.d:
सा तु सत्यमतिर्नित्यं शुचिर्विष्णुगृहे सती ।
नृत्यत्यत्यन्तसन्तुष्टा मनोज्ञा सञ्जुवादिनी ॥
1.20.m: And that virtuous Satyamatī, pure, highly delighted, charming, / and truthful in speech, danced continually in Viṣṇu’s temple.

1.20.s:
so 'pi rājā mahābhāgo dvādaśīddhādaśīdine /
dhvajamāropayatyeva manojñaṃ bahuvistaram //
1.20.d:
सो ऽपि राजा महाभागो द्वादशीद्धादशीदिने ।
ध्वजमारोपयत्येव मनोज्ञं बहुविस्तरम् ॥
1.20.m: That highly fortunate king, too, on every twelfth lunar day, / would hoist a beautiful, vast flag.

1.20.s:
evaṃ hariparaṃ nityaṃ rājānaṃ dharmakovidam /
primāṃ matyamatiṃ cāmya devā api sadāstuvan //
1.20.d:
एवं हरिपरं नित्यं राजानं धर्मकोविदम् ।
प्रिमां मत्यमतिं चाम्य देवा अपि सदास्तुवन् ॥
1.20.m: Thus, even the gods always praised that king who was ever devoted to Hari and skilled in righteousness, / as well as his beloved Satyamatī.

1.20.s:
triloke viśrutau jñātvā dampatī dharmako vidau /
āyayau bahubhiḥ śipyairdraṣṭukāmo vibhāṇḍakaḥ //
1.20.d:
त्रिलोके विश्रुतौ ज्ञात्वा दम्पती धर्मको विदौ ।
आययौ बहुभिः शिप्यैर्द्रष्टुकामो विभाण्डकः ॥
1.20.m: Knowing the couple to be renowned throughout the three worlds and skilled in righteousness, / Vibhāṇḍaka arrived, accompanied by many disciples, desiring to see them.

1.20.s:
tamāyāntaṃ muniṃ śrutvā sa tu rājā vibhāṇḍakam /
pratyudyayau sapatnīkaḥ prajā bhirbahuvistaram //
1.20.d:
तमायान्तं मुनिं श्रुत्वा स तु राजा विभाण्डकम् ।
प्रत्युद्ययौ सपत्नीकः प्रजा भिर्बहुविस्तरम् ॥
1.20.m: Hearing that the sage Vibhāṇḍaka was arriving, the king, / accompanied by his wife and a vast multitude of subjects, went out to meet him.

1.20.s:
kṛtātithyakriyaṃ śāntaṃ kṛtāsanaparigraham /
nīcāsanasthito bhūyaḥ prāñjalirmunimabravīt //
1.20.d:
कृतातिथ्यक्रियं शान्तं कृतासनपरिग्रहम् ।
नीचासनस्थितो भूयः प्राञ्जलिर्मुनिमब्रवीत् ॥
1.20.m: When [the sage], serene, had received hospitality and had taken his seat, / [the king], seated on a lower seat, spoke to the sage with folded hands:

1.20.s:
rājovāca
bhagavankṛtakṛtyo 'smiṃ tvadabhyāgamanena veṃ /
satāmāyamanaṃ santaṃ praśaṃsanti suravāvaham //
1.20.d:
राजोवाच
भगवन्कृतकृत्यो ऽस्मिं त्वदभ्यागमनेन वें ।
सतामायमनं सन्तं प्रशंसन्ति सुरवावहम् ॥
1.20.m: The king said: / O venerable one, I have fulfilled my life's purpose by your arrival; / the wise praise the coming of virtuous men as bringing welfare to all.

1.20.s:
yatra syānmahatāṃ prema tatra syuḥ sarvasampadaḥ /
tejaḥ kīrtirdhanaṃ putrā iti prahurvipaścitaḥ //
1.20.d:
यत्र स्यान्महतां प्रेम तत्र स्युः सर्वसम्पदः ।
तेजः कीर्तिर्धनं पुत्रा इति प्रहुर्विपश्चितः ॥
1.20.m: Where there is love from the great, there all prosperity resides— / splendour, fame, wealth, and sons—so the wise have declared.

1.20.s:
tatra vṛddhimupāyānti theyāṃsyanudinaṃ mune /
yatra santaḥ prakurvanti mahatīṃ karuṇāṃ prabho //
1.20.d:
तत्र वृद्धिमुपायान्ति थेयांस्यनुदिनं मुने ।
यत्र सन्तः प्रकुर्वन्ति महतीं करुणां प्रभो ॥
1.20.m: Auspicious blessings increase day by day, O sage, / wherever the virtuous bestow their great compassion, O master.

1.20.s:
yo mṛrdhni dhāgyedūhyanmahatpādajalaṃ rajaḥ /
sa snātaḥ sarvatīrtheṣu puṇyātmā nātra saṃśayaḥ //
1.20.d:
यो मृर्ध्नि धाग्येदूह्यन्महत्पादजलं रजः ।
स स्नातः सर्वतीर्थेषु पुण्यात्मा नात्र संशयः ॥
1.20.m: He who bears upon his head the water and dust from the feet of the great / has bathed in all the sacred fords; he is a meritorious soul, without a doubt.

1.20.s:
mama putrāśca dārāśca saṃpattvayi samarpitāḥ /
māmājñāpaya viprendra kiṃ priyaṃ karavāṇi te //
1.20.d:
मम पुत्राश्च दाराश्च संपत्त्वयि समर्पिताः ।
मामाज्ञापय विप्रेन्द्र किं प्रियं करवाणि ते ॥
1.20.m: My sons, my wife, and my wealth are surrendered to you; / command me, O foremost of brahmins, what pleasing deed I may perform for you.

1.20.s:
vinañcavanataṃ bhūpaṃ sa nirīkṣya munīśaavaraḥ /
spṛśaṣankareṇa taṃ prītyuvācātiharṣitaḥ //
1.20.d:
विनञ्चवनतं भूपं स निरीक्ष्य मुनीशअवरः ।
स्पृशषन्करेण तं प्रीत्युवाचातिहर्षितः ॥
1.20.m: Beholding the king bowed in humility, that lord among sages, / touching him with his hand, spoke with affectionate delight:

1.20.s:
ṛṣiruvāca
gajanyaduktaṃ bhavatā tatsarvaṃ tvatkulocitam /
vinayāvanataḥ sarvo bahuśreyo labhediha //
1.20.d:
ऋषिरुवाच
गजन्यदुक्तं भवता तत्सर्वं त्वत्कुलोचितम् ।
विनयावनतः सर्वो बहुश्रेयो लभेदिह ॥
1.20.m: The sage said: / O king, all that has been said by you is worthy of your lineage; / anyone humble with modesty attains great welfare in this world.

1.20.s:
dharmaścārthaśca kāmaśca mokṣaśca nṛpasattama /
vinayāllabhate martyo durlabhaṃ kiṃ mahātmanām //
1.20.d:
धर्मश्चार्थश्च कामश्च मोक्षश्च नृपसत्तम ।
विनयाल्लभते मर्त्यो दुर्लभं किं महात्मनाम् ॥
1.20.m: Righteousness, wealth, pleasure, and liberation, O best of kings— / a mortal attains these through humility; what is hard to attain for noble souls?

1.20.s:
prīto 'smi tava bhāpāla sanmārgaparivarttinaḥ /
svasti te satataṃ bhūyādyatpṛcchāmi taducyatām //
1.20.d:
प्रीतो ऽस्मि तव भापाल सन्मार्गपरिवर्त्तिनः ।
स्वस्ति ते सततं भूयाद्यत्पृच्छामि तदुच्यताम् ॥
1.20.m: I am pleased with you, O protector of the earth, walking in the right path. / May well-being always attend you; tell me what I ask.

1.20.s:
pūjā bahuvidhāḥ santi hastuṣṭividhāyikāḥ /
tāsu nityaṃ dhvajārope varttse tvaṃ sadodyataḥ //
1.20.d:
पूजा बहुविधाः सन्ति हस्तुष्टिविधायिकाः ।
तासु नित्यं ध्वजारोपे वर्त्त्से त्वं सदोद्यतः ॥
1.20.m: There are many kinds of worship that bring delight to Hari; / among them, you are ever intent and constantly engaged in hoisting a flag.

1.20.s:
bhāryāpi tava sādhvīyaṃ nityaṃ nṛtyaparāyaṇā /
kimarthametadvṛttāntaṃ yathāvadvaktumarhasi //
1.20.d:
भार्यापि तव साध्वीयं नित्यं नृत्यपरायणा ।
किमर्थमेतद्वृत्तान्तं यथावद्वक्तुमर्हसि ॥
1.20.m: This virtuous wife of yours, too, is constantly devoted to dancing. / You should relate to me this matter as it truly happened, and why.

1.20.s:
rājovāca
śṛṇuṣva bhagavansarvaṃ yatpṛcchasi vadāmi tat /
āścaryabhūtaṃ lokānāmāvayoścaritaṃ tviha //
1.20.d:
राजोवाच
शृणुष्व भगवन्सर्वं यत्पृच्छसि वदामि तत् ।
आश्चर्यभूतं लोकानामावयोश्चरितं त्विह ॥
1.20.m: The king said: / Listen, O lord; I shall tell you all that you ask, / which is a wondrous account of both of us in this world.

1.20.s:
ahamāsaṃ purā śūdro mālinirnāma sattama /
kumārgaganirato nityaṃ sarvalokāhike rataḥ //
1.20.d:
अहमासं पुरा शूद्रो मालिनिर्नाम सत्तम ।
कुमार्गगनिरतो नित्यं सर्वलोकाहिके रतः ॥
1.20.m: In a former birth I was a Śūdra named Mālin, O best of men, / always walking evil paths, intent on harming all people,

1.20.s:
piśuno dharmavidveṣī devadravyāpahārakaḥ /
godhnaśca brahmahā cauraḥ sarvaprāṇivadhe rataḥ //
1.20.d:
पिशुनो धर्मविद्वेषी देवद्रव्यापहारकः ।
गोध्नश्च ब्रह्महा चौरः सर्वप्राणिवधे रतः ॥
1.20.m: slanderous, hating righteousness, a plunderer of deities' property, / a cow-killer, a brahmin-slayer, a thief, bent on killing all living creatures,

1.20.s:
nityaṃ niṣṭhuravaktā ca pāpī veśyāparāyaṇaḥ /
evaṃ sthitaḥ kiyatkālamanāhatyaṃ mahadṛcaḥ //
1.20.d:
नित्यं निष्ठुरवक्ता च पापी वेश्यापरायणः ।
एवं स्थितः कियत्कालमनाहत्यं महदृचः ॥
1.20.m: habitually speaking harsh words, sinful, devoted to prostitutes. / Remaining thus for some time, disregarding the words of the great,

1.20.s:
sarvabandhuparityakto duḥkhī vanamupāgataḥ /
mṛgamāṃsāśano nityaṃ tathā pānthāvillampakaḥ //
1.20.d:
सर्वबन्धुपरित्यक्तो दुःखी वनमुपागतः ।
मृगमांसाशनो नित्यं तथा पान्थाविल्लम्पकः ॥
1.20.m: abandoned by all relatives and miserable, I went to the forest, / constantly eating the meat of deer and plundering wayfarers.

1.20.s:
ekākī duḥkhabahulo nyavasannirjane vane /
ekadā kṣutpariśrānto nidāghārttaḥ pipāsitaḥ //
1.20.d:
एकाकी दुःखबहुलो न्यवसन्निर्जने वने ।
एकदा क्षुत्परिश्रान्तो निदाघार्त्तः पिपासितः ॥
1.20.m: Solitary and laden with sorrow, I lived in an uninhabited forest. / Once, exhausted by hunger, afflicted by the heat of summer, and thirsty,

1.20.s:
jīrṇaṃ devālayaṃ viṣṇorapaśyaṃ vijane vane /
haṃsakāraṇḍavākīrṇaṃ tatsamīpe mahatsaraḥ //
1.20.d:
जीर्णं देवालयं विष्णोरपश्यं विजने वने ।
हंसकारण्डवाकीर्णं तत्समीपे महत्सरः ॥
1.20.m: I saw a ruined temple of Viṣṇu in the desolate forest, / and nearby a large lake teeming with swans and wild ducks,

1.20.s:
paryantavanapuṣpaughacchāditaṃ tanmunīśvara /
apibaṃ tatra pānīyaṃ tattīre vigataśramaḥ //
1.20.d:
पर्यन्तवनपुष्पौघच्छादितं तन्मुनीश्वर ।
अपिबं तत्र पानीयं तत्तीरे विगतश्रमः ॥
1.20.m: covered with a mass of wild forest flowers, O lord of sages. / I drank water there, and on its bank, my fatigue was dispelled.

1.20.s:
phalāni jagdhvā śīrṇāni svayaṃ kṣucca nivāritā /
tasmiñjīrṇīlaye viṣṇonarnivāsaṃ kṛtakavānaham //
1.20.d:
फलानि जग्ध्वा शीर्णानि स्वयं क्षुच्च निवारिता ।
तस्मिञ्जीर्णीलये विष्णोनर्निवासं कृतकवानहम् ॥
1.20.m: Eating fallen fruits, my hunger too was appeased; / and in that ruined abode of Viṣṇu, I took up my residence.

1.20.s:
jīrṇasphuṭitasaṃdhānaṃ tasya nityamakāriṣam /
parṇaistṛṇaiśca kāṣṭhaighair gṛhaṃ samyak prakalpitam //
1.20.d:
जीर्णस्फुटितसंधानं तस्य नित्यमकारिषम् ।
पर्णैस्तृणैश्च काष्ठैघैर् गृहं सम्यक् प्रकल्पितम् ॥
1.20.m: I constantly repaired whatever was broken and dilapidated in it; / with leaves, grasses, and piles of timber, I fashioned a dwelling properly.

1.20.s:
svasurārāthaṃ tu tadbhamirmayā litpā munīśvara /
tatrāhaṃ vyādhavṛttistho hatvā bahuvidhānmṛgān //
1.20.d:
स्वसुराराथं तु तद्भमिर्मया लित्पा मुनीश्वर ।
तत्राहं व्याधवृत्तिस्थो हत्वा बहुविधान्मृगान् ॥
1.20.m: For my own ease, O lord of sages, its floor was plastered by me. / There, pursuing the profession of a hunter, killing various kinds of deer,

1.20.s:
ājīvaṃ vartaya nnityaṃ varṣāṇāṃ viṃśatiḥ sthitaḥ /
atheyamāgatā sādhvī vindhyadeśasamudbhavā //
1.20.d:
आजीवं वर्तय न्नित्यं वर्षाणां विंशतिः स्थितः ।
अथेयमागता साध्वी विन्ध्यदेशसमुद्भवा ॥
1.20.m: I stayed for twenty years, continually maintaining my livelihood. / Then this virtuous woman arrived, born in the Vindhya region,

1.20.s:
niṣādakulajā viprā nānmā khyātā/ñavakokilā /
bandhuvargaparityaktā duḥkhitā jīrṇavigrahā //
1.20.d:
निषादकुलजा विप्रा नान्मा ख्याता।ञवकोकिला ।
बन्धुवर्गपरित्यक्ता दुःखिता जीर्णविग्रहा ॥
1.20.m: born of a Niṣāda family, O brāhmaṇa, known by the name Vakakokilā, / abandoned by her relatives, miserable, with an emaciated body,

1.20.s:
kṣuttṛḍgharmapariśrāntā śocantī svakṛtaṃ hyagham /
daivayogākatsamāyātābhramantī vijane vane //
1.20.d:
क्षुत्तृड्घर्मपरिश्रान्ता शोचन्ती स्वकृतं ह्यघम् ।
दैवयोगाकत्समायाताभ्रमन्ती विजने वने ॥
1.20.m: exhausted by hunger, thirst, and heat, grieving indeed for the evil deeds she had done, / having arrived by the turn of fate, wandering in the solitary forest,

1.20.s:
grīṣmatāpārdditā bāhye svānte cādhinipūḍitā /
imāṃ duḥkhārditāṃ dṛṣṭvā jātā me vipulā dayā //
1.20.d:
ग्रीष्मतापार्द्दिता बाह्ये स्वान्ते चाधिनिपूडिता ।
इमां दुःखार्दितां दृष्ट्वा जाता मे विपुला दया ॥
1.20.m: afflicted externally by the heat of summer and tormented internally by mental anguish. / Seeing her tormented by sorrow, immense compassion arose in me.

1.20.s:
dattaṃ mayā jalaṃ cāsyai māṃsaṃ vanyaphalāni ca /
gataśramātviyaṃ brahmanmayā pṛṣṭā yathā tayam //
1.20.d:
दत्तं मया जलं चास्यै मांसं वन्यफलानि च ।
गतश्रमात्वियं ब्रह्मन्मया पृष्टा यथा तयम् ॥
1.20.m: Water, meat, and wild fruits were given to her by me. / When her exhaustion was gone, O brāhmaṇa, she was asked by me as to the truth of the matter.

1.20.s:
avedayatsvavṛttāntaṃ tacchṛṇuṣva mahāmune /
nānmāvakokilā cāhaṃ niṣādakulasabhbhavā //
1.20.d:
अवेदयत्स्ववृत्तान्तं तच्छृणुष्व महामुने ।
नान्मावकोकिला चाहं निषादकुलसभ्भवा ॥
1.20.m: She related her own story; listen to that, O great sage: / 'I am Vakakokilā by name, born of a Niṣāda family,

1.20.s:
dārukasya sutā cāhaṃ vindhyaparvatavāsinī /
parasvahāriṇī nityaṃ sadā paiśunyavādinī //
1.20.d:
दारुकस्य सुता चाहं विन्ध्यपर्वतवासिनी ।
परस्वहारिणी नित्यं सदा पैशुन्यवादिनी ॥
1.20.m: and the daughter of Dāruka, residing on the Vindhya mountain, / constantly taking the property of others, always speaking slander.

1.20.s:
puṃścalūtyevamuktvā tu bandhuvargaiḥ samujjhitā /
kiyatkālaṃ tataḥ patyā bhṛtāhaṃ lokaninditā //
1.20.d:
पुंश्चलूत्येवमुक्त्वा तु बन्धुवर्गैः समुज्झिता ।
कियत्कालं ततः पत्या भृताहं लोकनिन्दिता ॥
1.20.m: Saying: "She is a wanton woman," I was cast out by my relatives. / Then for some time, condemned by people, I was maintained by my husband.

1.20.s:
daivātso 'pi gato lokaṃ yamasyātra vihāya mām /
kāntāre vijane caikā bhramantī duḥkhapīḍitā //
1.20.d:
दैवात्सो ऽपि गतो लोकं यमस्यात्र विहाय माम् ।
कान्तारे विजने चैका भ्रमन्ती दुःखपीडिता ॥
1.20.m: By fate, he too departed to the world of Yama, leaving me behind here. / Wandering alone in the solitary wild forest, afflicted with grief,

1.20.s:
daivāttvatsavidhaṃ prātpā jīvitāhaṃ tvayādhunā /
ityevaṃ svakṛtaṃ karma mahyaṃ sarvaṃ nyavedayat //
1.20.d:
दैवात्त्वत्सविधं प्रात्पा जीविताहं त्वयाधुना ।
इत्येवं स्वकृतं कर्म मह्यं सर्वं न्यवेदयत् ॥
1.20.m: by fate I arrived near you, and I have now been revived by you.' / In this way, she related to me all the deeds she had done.

1.20.s:
tato devālaye tasmindamapatībhāvamāśritau /
sthitau varṣāṇi daśa ca āvāṃ māṃsaphalāśinau //
1.20.d:
ततो देवालये तस्मिन्दमपतीभावमाश्रितौ ।
स्थितौ वर्षाणि दश च आवां मांसफलाशिनौ ॥
1.20.m: Then, having assumed the status of husband and wife in that temple of the god, / eating meat and fruits, the two of us lived there for ten years.

1.20.s:
ekadā madyapānena pramattau nirbharaimune /
tatra devālaye rāghatrau muditau māṃsabhojanāt //
1.20.d:
एकदा मद्यपानेन प्रमत्तौ निर्भरैमुने ।
तत्र देवालये राघत्रौ मुदितौ मांसभोजनात् ॥
1.20.m: Once, O sage, deeply intoxicated by drinking wine, / joyful from eating meat, at night in that temple of the god,

1.20.s:
tanuvastrāparijñānau nṛtyaṃ cakṛva mohitau /
prārabdhakarma bhogāntamāvāṃ yugapadāgatau //
1.20.d:
तनुवस्त्रापरिज्ञानौ नृत्यं चकृव मोहितौ ।
प्रारब्धकर्म भोगान्तमावां युगपदागतौ ॥
1.20.m: unconscious of our clothes, bewitched, we both danced. / We both reached the end of the experiencing of our commenced karma simultaneously.

1.20.s:
yamadūtāstadāyātāḥ pāśahastā bhayaṅkarāḥ /
netumāvāṃ nṛtyaratau sudhorāṃ yamayātanām //
1.20.d:
यमदूतास्तदायाताः पाशहस्ता भयङ्कराः ।
नेतुमावां नृत्यरतौ सुधोरां यमयातनाम् ॥
1.20.m: Then the messengers of Yama arrived, fearful, with nooses in hand, / to take us both, delighting in dance, to the exceedingly terrible torment of Yama.

1.20.s:
tataḥ prasanno bhagavānkarmaṇā mama mānada /
devāvasathasaṃskārasaṃjñitena kṛtena naḥ //
1.20.d:
ततः प्रसन्नो भगवान्कर्मणा मम मानद ।
देवावसथसंस्कारसंज्ञितेन कृतेन नः ॥
1.20.m: Then, O respect-giver, the Blessed Lord was pleased with my deed, / which was performed by us under the name of renovating the temple of the god.

1.20.s:
svadūtānprepayāmāsa svabhaktāvanatatparaḥ /
te dūtā devadevasya śaṅkhacakra gadādharāḥ //
1.20.d:
स्वदूतान्प्रेपयामास स्वभक्तावनतत्परः ।
ते दूता देवदेवस्य शङ्खचक्र गदाधराः ॥
1.20.m: Intent on protecting His own devotees, He sent His messengers. / Those messengers of the God of gods, holding the conch, discus, and mace,

1.20.s:
sahasrasūryāsaṃkāśāḥ sarve cārucaturbhujāḥ /
kirīṭakuṇḍaladharā hāriṇo vanamālinaḥ //
1.20.d:
सहस्रसूर्यासंकाशाः सर्वे चारुचतुर्भुजाः ।
किरीटकुण्डलधरा हारिणो वनमालिनः ॥
1.20.m: resembling a thousand suns, all having handsome four arms, / wearing diadems and earrings, charming, wearing forest garlands,

1.20.s:
diśo vitimirā vipra kurvantaḥ svena tejasā /
bhayaṅkarānyāśahastāndaṃṣṭriṇo yamakiṅkarān //
1.20.d:
दिशो वितिमिरा विप्र कुर्वन्तः स्वेन तेजसा ।
भयङ्करान्याशहस्तान्दंष्ट्रिणो यमकिङ्करान् ॥
1.20.m: dispelling the darkness from the directions, O brāhmaṇa, with their own splendor, / to the terrifying, fanged servants of Yama with nooses in hand,

1.20.s: āvayogrāhaṇe yattānṛcuḥ kṛṣṇaparāyaṇāḥ //
1.20.d: आवयोग्राहणे यत्तानृचुः कृष्णपरायणाः ॥
1.20.m: who were intent on seizing the two of us, those devoted to Kṛṣṇa spoke:

1.20.s:
viṣṇudūtā ūcuḥ
bho bho krūrā dūrācārā vivekaparivarjitāḥ /
muñcadhvametau niṣpāpau dampatī harivallabhau //
1.20.d:
विष्णुदूता ऊचुः
भो भो क्रूरा दूराचारा विवेकपरिवर्जिताः ।
मुञ्चध्वमेतौ निष्पापौ दम्पती हरिवल्लभौ ॥
1.20.m: The messengers of Viṣṇu said: / 'Ho, ho! Cruel ones, of wicked conduct, devoid of discernment, / release these two sinless ones, a husband and wife dear to Hari!

1.20.s:
vivekastriṣu lokeṣu saṃpadāmādikāraṇam /
apāpe pāpadhīryastu taṃ vidyātpuruṣādhamam //
1.20.d:
विवेकस्त्रिषु लोकेषु संपदामादिकारणम् ।
अपापे पापधीर्यस्तु तं विद्यात्पुरुषाधमम् ॥
1.20.m: Discernment is the prime cause of prosperity in the three worlds. / But he who views the sinless as sinful, one should know him as the lowest of men.

1.20.s: pāpe tvapāpadhīryastu taṃ vidyādadhamādhamam //
1.20.d: पापे त्वपापधीर्यस्तु तं विद्यादधमाधमम् ॥
1.20.m: And he who views the sinful as sinless, one should know him as the lowest of the low!'

1.20.s:
yamadūtā ūcuḥ
yuṣmābhiḥ satyamevoktaṃ kiṃ tvetau pāpisattamau /
yamena pāpino daṇḍyāstanneṣyāmo vayaṃ tvimau //
1.20.d:
यमदूता ऊचुः
युष्माभिः सत्यमेवोक्तं किं त्वेतौ पापिसत्तमौ ।
यमेन पापिनो दण्ड्यास्तन्नेष्यामो वयं त्विमौ ॥
1.20.m: The messengers of Yama said: / 'What you have said is indeed true, but these two are the greatest of sinners. / Sinners must be punished by Yama; therefore, we will take these two.

1.20.s:
śrutipraṇihito dharmo hyadharmastadviparyayaḥ /
dharmādharmaviveko 'yaṃ tanneṣyāmo yamāntikam //
1.20.d:
श्रुतिप्रणिहितो धर्मो ह्यधर्मस्तद्विपर्ययः ।
धर्माधर्मविवेको ऽयं तन्नेष्यामो यमान्तिकम् ॥
1.20.m: Dharma is what is enjoined by the scriptures, and adharma is its opposite. / This is the discernment of dharma and adharma; therefore, we will lead them to the presence of Yama.'

1.20.s:
etactchuvātikupitā viṣṇudūtā mahaujasaḥ /
pratyūcūstānyamabhaṭānadharme dharmamāninaḥ //
1.20.d:
एतच्त्छुवातिकुपिता विष्णुदूता महौजसः ।
प्रत्यूचूस्तान्यमभटानधर्मे धर्ममानिनः ॥
1.20.m: Hearing this, the exceedingly mighty messengers of Viṣṇu became very angry, / and replied to those soldiers of Yama who considered adharma as dharma:

1.20.s:
viṣṇadūtā ūcuḥ
aho kaṣṭaṃ dharmadṛśāmadharmaḥ spṛśate sabhām /
samyagvivekaśūnyānāṃ nidānaṃ hyāpadāṃ mahat //
1.20.d:
विष्णदूता ऊचुः
अहो कष्टं धर्मदृशामधर्मः स्पृशते सभाम् ।
सम्यग्विवेकशून्यानां निदानं ह्यापदां महत् ॥
1.20.m: The messengers of Viṣṇu said: / 'Alas, the tragedy! Adharma touches the assembly of those who perceive dharma. / For those utterly devoid of discernment, it is indeed the great source of disasters.

1.20.s:
tarkāṇādyaviśeṣeṇa narakādhyakṣatāṃ gatāḥ /
yūyaṃ kimarthamadyāpi karttuṃ pāpāni sodyamāḥ //
1.20.d:
तर्काणाद्यविशेषेण नरकाध्यक्षतां गताः ।
यूयं किमर्थमद्यापि कर्त्तुं पापानि सोद्यमाः ॥
1.20.m: Having attained the directorship of hell through the lack of discrimination in reasoning and the like, / why are you, even today, eager to commit sins?

1.20.s:
svakarmakṣayaparyantaṃ mahāpātakino 'pi ca /
tiṣṭanti narake ghore yāvaccandrārkatārakam //
1.20.d:
स्वकर्मक्षयपर्यन्तं महापातकिनो ऽपि च ।
तिष्टन्ति नरके घोरे यावच्चन्द्रार्कतारकम् ॥
1.20.m: Even great sinners, until the exhaustion of their own karma, / stay in the terrible hell as long as the moon, sun, and stars endure.

1.20.s:
pūrvasaṃcitapāpānāmadṛṣṭvā niṣkṛtiṃ vṛthā /
kimarthaṃ pāpakarmāṇi kariṣye 'tha punaḥ punaḥ //
1.20.d:
पूर्वसंचितपापानामदृष्ट्वा निष्कृतिं वृथा ।
किमर्थं पापकर्माणि करिष्ये ऽथ पुनः पुनः ॥
1.20.m: Not seeing expiation for sins accumulated in the past, / why would one vainly commit sinful acts again and again?

1.20.s:
śrutipraṇihito dharmaḥ satyaṃ satyaṃ na saṃśayaḥ /
kintvābhyāṃ caritāndharmānpravakṣyāmo yathātatham //
1.20.d:
श्रुतिप्रणिहितो धर्मः सत्यं सत्यं न संशयः ।
किन्त्वाभ्यां चरितान्धर्मान्प्रवक्ष्यामो यथातथम् ॥
1.20.m: Dharma is enjoined by the scriptures—true, true, there is no doubt. / But we shall explain as it is the dharmas practiced by these two.

1.20.s:
etau pāpavinirmuktau hariśuśrūṣaṇe ratau /
hariṇā trāyamāṇau ca muñcadhvamavilambitam //
1.20.d:
एतौ पापविनिर्मुक्तौ हरिशुश्रूषणे रतौ ।
हरिणा त्रायमाणौ च मुञ्चध्वमविलम्बितम् ॥
1.20.m: These two are free from sin, devoted to the service of Hari, / and are being protected by Hari. Release them without delay!

1.20.s:
eṣā ca nartanaṃ cakre tathaiva dhvajaroṣaṇam /
antakāle viṣṇugṛhe tena niṣpāpatāṃ gatau //
1.20.d:
एषा च नर्तनं चक्रे तथैव ध्वजरोषणम् ।
अन्तकाले विष्णुगृहे तेन निष्पापतां गतौ ॥
1.20.m: She danced, and likewise raised a flag / at the time of death in the house of Viṣṇu; through that, they both attained sinlessness.

1.20.s:
antakāle tu yannāma śrutvoktvāpi ca vai sakṛt /
labhate paramaṃ sthānaṃ kimu śūśrūṣaṇe ratāḥ //
1.20.d:
अन्तकाले तु यन्नाम श्रुत्वोक्त्वापि च वै सकृत् ।
लभते परमं स्थानं किमु शूश्रूषणे रताः ॥
1.20.m: Even at the time of death, having heard or spoken His name even once, / one attains the supreme place; how much more so those devoted to His service?

1.20.s:
mahāpātakayukto vā yukto vāpyupapātakaiḥ /./
kṛṣṇasevī naro 'nte 'pi labhate paramāṃ gatim //
1.20.d:
महापातकयुक्तो वा युक्तो वाप्युपपातकैः ॥।
कृष्णसेवी नरो ऽन्ते ऽपि लभते परमां गतिम् ॥
1.20.m: Whether endowed with mortal sins or endowed with minor sins, / a man who serves Kṛṣṇa, even at the end, attains the supreme destination.

1.20.s:
yatīnāṃ viṣṇubhaktānāṃ paricaryā parāyaṇāḥ /
te dūtāḥ sahasā yānti pāpino 'pi parāṃ gatim //
1.20.d:
यतीनां विष्णुभक्तानां परिचर्या परायणाः ।
ते दूताः सहसा यान्ति पापिनो ऽपि परां गतिम् ॥
1.20.m: Those devoted to the service of ascetics who are devotees of Viṣṇu, / O messengers, even if sinful, go quickly to the supreme destination.

1.20.s:
muhurtaṃ vā muhurtārddhaṃ yastiṣṭoddharimandire /
so 'pi yāti paraṃ sthānaṃ kimudvātraghiṃśavatsarān //
1.20.d:
मुहुर्तं वा मुहुर्तार्द्धं यस्तिष्टोद्धरिमन्दिरे ।
सो ऽपि याति परं स्थानं किमुद्वात्रघिंशवत्सरान् ॥
1.20.m: He who stays in the temple of Hari for a muhūrta or half a muhūrta, / he too goes to the supreme place; how much more so for thirty-two years?

1.20.s:
upalepanakarttārau saṃmārjanaparāyaṇau /
etau harigṛhe nityaṃ jīrṇaśīrṇādhiropakau //
1.20.d:
उपलेपनकर्त्तारौ संमार्जनपरायणौ ।
एतौ हरिगृहे नित्यं जीर्णशीर्णाधिरोपकौ ॥
1.20.m: They were performers of plastering, devoted to sweeping, / constantly repairing whatever was dilapidated and broken in the house of Hari.

1.20.s:
jalasecanakarttārau dīpadau harimandire /
kathametau mahābhāgau yātanābhogamarhatha //
1.20.d:
जलसेचनकर्त्तारौ दीपदौ हरिमन्दिरे ।
कथमेतौ महाभागौ यातनाभोगमर्हथ ॥
1.20.m: They were sprinklers of water, givers of lamps in the temple of Hari. / How do these two highly fortunate ones deserve the experience of torture?'

1.20.s:
ityuktā viṣṇudūtāste cchitvā pāśāṃstadaiva hi /
āropyāvāṃ vimānāgrayaṃ yayurviṣṇoḥ paraṃ padam //
1.20.d:
इत्युक्ता विष्णुदूतास्ते च्छित्वा पाशांस्तदैव हि ।
आरोप्यावां विमानाग्रयं ययुर्विष्णोः परं पदम् ॥
1.20.m: Thus addressed, those messengers of Viṣṇu cut the nooses at that very moment, / placed the two of us on a splendid aerial chariot, and went to the supreme abode of Viṣṇu.

1.20.s:
tatra sāmīpyamāpannau devadevasya cakriṇaḥ /
divyānbhogānbhuktavantau tāvatkālaṃ munīśvara //
1.20.d:
तत्र सामीप्यमापन्नौ देवदेवस्य चक्रिणः ।
दिव्यान्भोगान्भुक्तवन्तौ तावत्कालं मुनीश्वर ॥
1.20.m: There, having attained proximity to the God of gods who bears the discus, / we enjoyed divine pleasures for that long period of time, O lord of sages.

1.20.s:
divyānbhogāṃstu tatrāpi bhuktvā yātau mahīmimām /
atrāpi saṃpadatulā harisevāprasādataḥ //
1.20.d:
दिव्यान्भोगांस्तु तत्रापि भुक्त्वा यातौ महीमिमाम् ।
अत्रापि संपदतुला हरिसेवाप्रसादतः ॥
1.20.m: Having enjoyed divine pleasures even there, we came to this earth; / here too is unequaled prosperity, by the grace of the service of Hari.

1.20.s:
anicchayā kṛtenāpi sevanena harermune /
prātpamīdṛk phalaṃ vipra devānāmapi durlabham //
1.20.d:
अनिच्छया कृतेनापि सेवनेन हरेर्मुने ।
प्रात्पमीदृक् फलं विप्र देवानामपि दुर्लभम् ॥
1.20.m: Even by service done to Hari without intention, O sage, / such a fruit has been attained, O brāhmaṇa, which is difficult even for the gods to attain.

1.20.s:
icchayārādhya viśveśaṃ bhaktibhāvena mādhavam /
prāpsyāvaḥ paramaṃ śreya iti heturnirupitaḥ //
1.20.d:
इच्छयाराध्य विश्वेशं भक्तिभावेन माधवम् ।
प्राप्स्यावः परमं श्रेय इति हेतुर्निरुपितः ॥
1.20.m: Having worshiped the Lord of the universe, Mādhava, with intention and a spirit of devotion, / we shall attain the supreme good—thus was the purpose determined.

1.20.s:
avaśenāpi yatkarma kṛtaṃ syātsumahatphalam /
jāyate bhūmidevendra kiṃ punaḥ śraddhayā kṛtam //
1.20.d:
अवशेनापि यत्कर्म कृतं स्यात्सुमहत्फलम् ।
जायते भूमिदेवेन्द्र किं पुनः श्रद्धया कृतम् ॥
1.20.m: Even what act is done involuntarily yields a very great fruit, / O best of earthly gods; how much more so that which is done with faith!

1.20.s:
etaduktaṃ niśamyāsau sa munīndro vibhaṇḍakaḥ /
praśasya dampatī tau tu prayayau svatapevanam //
1.20.d:
एतदुक्तं निशम्यासौ स मुनीन्द्रो विभण्डकः ।
प्रशस्य दम्पती तौ तु प्रययौ स्वतपेवनम् ॥
1.20.m: Hearing this speech, that Vibhaṇḍaka, the best of sages, / praised that couple and set out for his own penance-grove.

1.20.s:
tasmājjānīhi devarṣe devadevasya cakriṇaḥ /
paricaryā tu sarveṣāṃ kāmadhenūpamā smṛtā //
1.20.d:
तस्माज्जानीहि देवर्षे देवदेवस्य चक्रिणः ।
परिचर्या तु सर्वेषां कामधेनूपमा स्मृता ॥
1.20.m: Therefore know, O divine sage, that service to the God of gods who bears the discus / is remembered as being like the wish-fulfilling cow for all.

1.20.s:
haripūjāparāṇāṃ tu harireva sanātanaḥ /
dadāti paramaṃ śreyaḥ sarvakāmaphalamapradaḥ //
1.20.d:
हरिपूजापराणां तु हरिरेव सनातनः ।
ददाति परमं श्रेयः सर्वकामफलमप्रदः ॥
1.20.m: To those devoted to the worship of Hari, eternal Hari alone, / the bestower of the fruits of all desires, gives the supreme good.

1.20.s:
ya idaṃ puṇyamākhyānaṃ sarvapāpapraṇāśanam /
paṭhecca śṛṇuyādvāpi so 'pi yāti parāṃ rātim //
iti śrabṛhannāradīyaparāṇe pūrvabhāge prathamapāde sumatibhūpakathāvarṇanaṃ nāma viṃśa'dhyāyaḥ
1.20.d:
य इदं पुण्यमाख्यानं सर्वपापप्रणाशनम् ।
पठेच्च शृणुयाद्वापि सो ऽपि याति परां रातिम् ॥
इति श्रबृहन्नारदीयपराणे पूर्वभागे प्रथमपादे सुमतिभूपकथावर्णनं नाम विंशऽध्यायः
1.20.m:
Whoever reads or hears this meritorious narrative, which destroys all sins, / he too attains supreme delight.

Thus ends the twentieth chapter, titled “Description of the Story of King Sumati,” in the first quarter of the first part of the venerable Bṛhannāradīyapurāṇa.

1.21.s:
sanaka uvāca
anyadvūtaṃ pravakṣyāmi śṛṇu nārada tattvataḥ /
durlabhaṃ sarvalokeṣu vikhyātaṃ haripañcakam //
1.21.d:
सनक उवाच
अन्यद्वूतं प्रवक्ष्यामि शृणु नारद तत्त्वतः ।
दुर्लभं सर्वलोकेषु विख्यातं हरिपञ्चकम् ॥
1.21.m: Sanaka said: / I shall declare another vow, hear it in truth, O Nārada, / rare in all the worlds, renowned as the Haripañcaka.

1.21.s:
nārīṇāṃ ca narāṇāṃ ca sarvaduḥkhanivāraṇam /
dharmakāmārthamokṣāṇāṃ nidānaṃ munisattama //
1.21.d:
नारीणां च नराणां च सर्वदुःखनिवारणम् ।
धर्मकामार्थमोक्षाणां निदानं मुनिसत्तम ॥
1.21.m: It dispels all suffering for women and men; / it is the root cause of righteousness, pleasure, wealth, and liberation, O best of sages.

1.21.s:
sarvābhīṣṭapradaṃ caiva sarvavrataphalapradam /
mārgaśīrṣe site pakṣe daśamyāṃ niyatendriyaḥ //
1.21.d:
सर्वाभीष्टप्रदं चैव सर्वव्रतफलप्रदम् ।
मार्गशीर्षे सिते पक्षे दशम्यां नियतेन्द्रियः ॥
1.21.m: It grants all desires and gives the fruit of all vows. / In the bright fortnight of Mārgaśīrṣa, on the tenth day, with senses restrained,

1.21.s:
kuryātsnānādikaṃ karma dantadhāvanapūrvakama /
kṛtvā devārcanaṃ samyaktathā pañca mahādhvarān //
1.21.d:
कुर्यात्स्नानादिकं कर्म दन्तधावनपूर्वकम ।
कृत्वा देवार्चनं सम्यक्तथा पञ्च महाध्वरान् ॥
1.21.m: one should perform bath and other rites, preceded by cleaning the teeth, / having properly performed the worship of the deity, as well as the five great sacrifices.

1.21.s:
ekāśī ca bhavettasmin dine niyamamāsthitāḥ /
tataḥ prātaḥ samutthāya hyekādaśyāṃ munīśvaraḥ //
1.21.d:
एकाशी च भवेत्तस्मिन् दिने नियममास्थिताः ।
ततः प्रातः समुत्थाय ह्येकादश्यां मुनीश्वरः ॥
1.21.m: One should eat only once on that day, remaining firm in the observance. / Then rising early in the morning on the eleventh day, O lord of sages,

1.21.s:
snānaṃ kṛtvā yathācāraṃ hariṃ caivāryadṛhe /
snāpayeddevadeveśaṃ pañcāmṛtavidhānataḥ //
1.21.d:
स्नानं कृत्वा यथाचारं हरिं चैवार्यदृहे ।
स्नापयेद्देवदेवेशं पञ्चामृतविधानतः ॥
1.21.m: having bathed according to custom and [worshipped] Hari in one's home, / one should bathe the god of gods according to the rite of the fivefold nectar (pañcāmṛta).

1.21.s:
arcayetparayā bhaktyā gandhapuṣpādibhiḥ ṛmāt /
dhūpairdīpeśca naivaidyaistāmbūlaiśca pradakṣiṇaiḥ //
1.21.d:
अर्चयेत्परया भक्त्या गन्धपुष्पादिभिः ऋमात् ।
धूपैर्दीपेश्च नैवैद्यैस्ताम्बूलैश्च प्रदक्षिणैः ॥
1.21.m: One should worship [him] with supreme devotion in sequence with perfume, flowers, and the like, / with incense, lamps, food offerings, betel leaves, and circumambulations.

1.21.s:
saṃpūjya devadeveśamimaṃ mantramudīrayet /.
namaste ghajñānarupāya jñānadāya namo 'stute //
1.21.d:
संपूज्य देवदेवेशमिमं मन्त्रमुदीरयेत् ॥
नमस्ते घज्ञानरुपाय ज्ञानदाय नमो ऽस्तुते ॥
1.21.m: Having worshipped the god of gods, one should utter this mantra: / “Salutations to you whose form is knowledge! Salutations to you who grant knowledge!

1.21.s:
namaste sravaparupāya sarvasiddhipradāyine /
evaṃ praṇamya deveśaṃ vāsudevaṃ janārjanam //
1.21.d:
नमस्ते स्रवपरुपाय सर्वसिद्धिप्रदायिने ।
एवं प्रणम्य देवेशं वासुदेवं जनार्जनम् ॥
1.21.m: Salutations to you whose form is the universe! Salutations to the granter of all perfections!” / Having thus bowed down to the lord of gods, Vāsudeva, Janārdana,

1.21.s:
vakṣyamāṇena mantreṇa hyupavāsaṃ samarpayet /
pañcarātraṃ nirāhāro hyadyaprabhṛti keśava //
1.21.d:
वक्ष्यमाणेन मन्त्रेण ह्युपवासं समर्पयेत् ।
पञ्चरात्रं निराहारो ह्यद्यप्रभृति केशव ॥
1.21.m: one should dedicate the fast with the mantra that is to be stated: / “Remaining without food for five nights from today onward, O Keśava,

1.21.s:
tvadajñayā jagatsvāminmamābhīṣṭaprado bhava /
evaṃ samapya devasya upavāsaṃ jitendriyaḥ //
1.21.d:
त्वदज्ञया जगत्स्वामिन्ममाभीष्टप्रदो भव ।
एवं समप्य देवस्य उपवासं जितेन्द्रियः ॥
1.21.m: by your command, O Master of the universe, become the granter of my desire!” / Having thus dedicated the fast of the deity, with senses conquered,

1.21.s:
rātrau jāgaraṇaṃ kuryādekādaśyāmatho dvija /
dvādaśyāṃ ca trayodaśyāṃ caturdaśyāṃ jitendriyaḥ //
1.21.d:
रात्रौ जागरणं कुर्यादेकादश्यामथो द्विज ।
द्वादश्यां च त्रयोदश्यां चतुर्दश्यां जितेन्द्रियः ॥
1.21.m: one should keep a vigil at night on the eleventh day, then, O twice-born; / and on the twelfth, on the thirteenth, on the fourteenth, with senses controlled,

1.21.s:
paurṇanamāsyāṃ ca karttavyamevaṃ viṣṇvarcanaṃ mune /
ekādaśyāṃ paurṇamāsyāṃ karttavyaṃ jāgaraṃ tathā //
1.21.d:
पौर्णनमास्यां च कर्त्तव्यमेवं विष्ण्वर्चनं मुने ।
एकादश्यां पौर्णमास्यां कर्त्तव्यं जागरं तथा ॥
1.21.m: and on the full-moon day, such worship of Viṣṇu is to be performed, O sage. / On the eleventh and on the full-moon day, a vigil is likewise to be kept.

1.21.s:
pañcāmṛtādipūjā tu sāmānyā dinapañcasu /
kṣīreṇa snāpayedviṣṇuṃ paurṇamāsyāṃ tu śaktitaḥ /
tilahomaśca karttavyastiladānaṃ tathaiva ca //
1.21.d:
पञ्चामृतादिपूजा तु सामान्या दिनपञ्चसु ।
क्षीरेण स्नापयेद्विष्णुं पौर्णमास्यां तु शक्तितः ।
तिलहोमश्च कर्त्तव्यस्तिलदानं तथैव च ॥
1.21.m: The worship with the fivefold nectar and the like is common to all five days. / On the full-moon day, however, according to one's ability, one should bathe Viṣṇu with milk; / a sesame fire-oblation is to be performed, and likewise a gift of sesame.

1.21.s:
tataḥ ṣaṣṭe dine prātpe nirvatyaṃ svāśramakriyām /
saṃprāśya pañcagavyaṃ ca pūjayedvidhibaddharim //
1.21.d:
ततः षष्टे दिने प्रात्पे निर्वत्यं स्वाश्रमक्रियाम् ।
संप्राश्य पञ्चगव्यं च पूजयेद्विधिबद्धरिम् ॥
