1.21.m: Then on the sixth day, in the morning, having performed the rites of one's stage of life, / and having consumed the five products of the cow (pañcagavya), one should worship Hari according to rule.

1.21.s:
brāhmaṇānbhojayetpaścādvibhave satyavāritam /
tataḥ svabandhubhiḥ sārddhaṃ svayaṃ bhuñjīta vāgyataḥ //
1.21.d:
ब्राह्मणान्भोजयेत्पश्चाद्विभवे सत्यवारितम् ।
ततः स्वबन्धुभिः सार्द्धं स्वयं भुञ्जीत वाग्यतः ॥
1.21.m: Afterward, if means allow, one should feed brāhmaṇas without restriction; / then, restrained in speech, one should eat oneself along with one's kin.

1.21.s:
evaṃ paupādimāseṣu kārttikānteṣu nārada /
śuklapakṣe vrataṃ kuryātpūrvamivavidhinā naraḥ //
1.21.d:
एवं पौपादिमासेषु कार्त्तिकान्तेषु नारद ।
शुक्लपक्षे व्रतं कुर्यात्पूर्वमिवविधिना नरः ॥
1.21.m: In this way, in the months beginning with Pauṣa and ending with Kārttika, O Nārada, / in the bright fortnight, a man should observe the vow according to the previous rule.

1.21.s:
evaṃ saṃvatsaraṃ kāryaṃ vrataṃ pāpapraṇāśanam /
punaḥ prātpe mārgaśīrṣe kuryādudyapanaṃ vratī //
1.21.d:
एवं संवत्सरं कार्यं व्रतं पापप्रणाशनम् ।
पुनः प्रात्पे मार्गशीर्षे कुर्यादुद्यपनं व्रती ॥
1.21.m: In this manner the sin-destroying vow is to be performed for a year. / When Mārgaśīrṣa has arrived again, the observer of the vow should perform the concluding ceremony (udyāpana).

1.21.s:
dvija /
ekādaśyāṃ nirāhāro bhavetpūrvamiva dvija /
dvādaśyāṃ pañcagavyaṃ ca prāśayetsusamāhitaḥ //
1.21.d:
द्विज ।
एकादश्यां निराहारो भवेत्पूर्वमिव द्विज ।
द्वादश्यां पञ्चगव्यं च प्राशयेत्सुसमाहितः ॥
1.21.m:
O twice-born,
On the eleventh day, one should fast just as before, O twice-born; / and on the twelfth day, with a well-concentrated mind, one should consume the five products of the cow.

1.21.s:
gandhapuṣpā dibhiḥ samyagdevadevaṃ janārdanam /
abhyarcyopāyanaṃ dadyādrūhyaṇāya jitendriyaḥ //
1.21.d:
गन्धपुष्पा दिभिः सम्यग्देवदेवं जनार्दनम् ।
अभ्यर्च्योपायनं दद्याद्रूह्यणाय जितेन्द्रियः ॥
1.21.m: Having properly worshipped the god of gods, Janārdana, with perfume, flowers, and the like, / with restrained senses one should give a gift to a brāhmaṇa:

1.21.s:
pāyasaṃ madhusaṃmiśraṃ ghṛtayuktaṃ phalānvitam /
sugandhaja lasaṃyuktaṃ pūrṇakumbhaṃ sadakṣiṇam //
1.21.d:
पायसं मधुसंमिश्रं घृतयुक्तं फलान्वितम् ।
सुगन्धज लसंयुक्तं पूर्णकुम्भं सदक्षिणम् ॥
1.21.m: milk-rice mixed with honey, endowed with clarified butter, accompanied by fruits, / and a full jar filled with fragrant water along with a sacrificial fee,

1.21.s:
vastreṇācchāditaṃ kumbhaṃ pañcarantasamanvitam /
dadyādadhyātmaviduṣe brāhmaṇāya munīśvara //
1.21.d:
वस्त्रेणाच्छादितं कुम्भं पञ्चरन्तसमन्वितम् ।
दद्यादध्यात्मविदुषे ब्राह्मणाय मुनीश्वर ॥
1.21.m: a jar covered with a cloth, accompanied by the five jewels, / one should give to a brāhmaṇa who knows the supreme Self, O lord of sages.

1.21.s:
sarvātman sarvabhūteśa sarvavyāpinsanātana /
paramānnapradānena suprīto bhava mādhava //
1.21.d:
सर्वात्मन् सर्वभूतेश सर्वव्यापिन्सनातन ।
परमान्नप्रदानेन सुप्रीतो भव माधव ॥
1.21.m: “O Self of all, O Lord of all beings, O all-pervading, eternal one! / Through this gift of supreme food, be well pleased, O Mādhava!”

1.21.s:
anena pāyasaṃ dattvā brāhmaṇānbhojayettataḥ /
śaktito bandhubhiḥ sārddhaṃ svayaṃ bhuñjīta vāgyataḥ //
1.21.d:
अनेन पायसं दत्त्वा ब्राह्मणान्भोजयेत्ततः ।
शक्तितो बन्धुभिः सार्द्धं स्वयं भुञ्जीत वाग्यतः ॥
1.21.m: Having given the milk-rice with this [mantra], one should then feed brāhmaṇas; / according to one's ability, one should eat oneself along with kin, restrained in speech.

1.21.s:
vratametattu yaḥ kuryāddharipañcakasaṃjñitam /
na tasya punarāvṛttirbrahmalokātkadācana //
1.21.d:
व्रतमेतत्तु यः कुर्याद्धरिपञ्चकसंज्ञितम् ।
न तस्य पुनरावृत्तिर्ब्रह्मलोकात्कदाचन ॥
1.21.m: Whoever performs this vow named Haripañcaka, / for him there is never any return from the world of Brahmā.

1.21.s:
vratametatprakarttavya micchadbhirmokṣamuttam /
samastapāpakāntāradāvānalasamaṃ dvija //
1.21.d:
व्रतमेतत्प्रकर्त्तव्य मिच्छद्भिर्मोक्षमुत्तम् ।
समस्तपापकान्तारदावानलसमं द्विज ॥
1.21.m: This vow is to be undertaken by those desiring supreme liberation; / it is equal to a forest fire for the wilderness of all sins, O twice-born.

1.21.s:
gavāṃ koṭisahasrāṇi dattvā yatphalamāpnuyāt /
tatphalaṃ labhyate pumbhiretasmā dupavāsataḥ //
1.21.d:
गवां कोटिसहस्राणि दत्त्वा यत्फलमाप्नुयात् ।
तत्फलं लभ्यते पुम्भिरेतस्मा दुपवासतः ॥
1.21.m: Whatever fruit one obtains by giving thousands of crores of cows, / that fruit is obtained by men from this fast.

1.21.s:
yastvetacchṛṇuyādbhaktyā nārāyaṇaparāyaṇaḥ /
sa mucyate mahāghoraiḥ tāpakānāṃ ca koṭibhiḥ //
iti śrībṛhannāṃradīyapurāṇaṃ pūrvabhāge prathamapāde vratākhyāne mārgaśīrṣaśulkaikādaśīmāsabhya paurṇimāparyantaṃ pañcarātrivrataṃ nāmaikaviṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ
1.21.d:
यस्त्वेतच्छृणुयाद्भक्त्या नारायणपरायणः ।
स मुच्यते महाघोरैः तापकानां च कोटिभिः ॥
इति श्रीबृहन्नांरदीयपुराणं पूर्वभागे प्रथमपादे व्रताख्याने मार्गशीर्षशुल्कैकादशीमासभ्य पौर्णिमापर्यन्तं पञ्चरात्रिव्रतं नामैकविंशो ऽध्यायः
1.21.m:
Whoever listens to this with devotion, dedicated to Nārāyaṇa, / is freed from tens of millions of exceedingly terrible torments.

Thus ends the twenty-first chapter, titled “The Five-Night Vow from the Bright Eleventh to the Full Moon of Mārgaśīrṣa in the Narrative of Vows,” in the first quarter of the first part of the venerable Bṛhannāradīyapurāṇa.

1.22.s:
sanaka uvāca
anyad vratavaraṃ vakṣye tacchṛṇuṣva samāhitaḥ /
sarvāpāpaharaṃ puṇyaṃ sarvalokopakārakam //
1.22.d:
सनक उवाच
अन्यद् व्रतवरं वक्ष्ये तच्छृणुष्व समाहितः ।
सर्वापापहरं पुण्यं सर्वलोकोपकारकम् ॥
1.22.m: Sanaka said: / I shall declare another excellent vow; listen to it attentively, / pure, destroying all sins, beneficial to all the world.

1.22.s:
āṣāḍhre śrāvaṇe vāpi tathā bhādrapade 'pi ca /
tathaivāśvinake māse kuryādetadvataṃ dvija //
1.22.d:
आषाढ्रे श्रावणे वापि तथा भाद्रपदे ऽपि च ।
तथैवाश्विनके मासे कुर्यादेतद्वतं द्विज ॥
1.22.m: In Āṣāḍha or in Śrāvaṇa, and also in Bhādrapada, / or likewise in the month of Āśvina, one should perform this vow, O twice-born.

1.22.s:
eteṣvanyatame māse śulkapakṣe jitendriyaḥ /
prāśayetpañcagavyaṃ ca svapedviṣṇusamīpataḥ //
1.22.d:
एतेष्वन्यतमे मासे शुल्कपक्षे जितेन्द्रियः ।
प्राशयेत्पञ्चगव्यं च स्वपेद्विष्णुसमीपतः ॥
1.22.m: In any of these months, in the bright fortnight, with senses conquered, / one should consume the five products of the cow (pañcagavya) and sleep near Viṣṇu.

1.22.s:
tataḥ prātaḥ samutthāya nityakarma samāpya ca /
śraddhayā pūjayedviṣṇuṃ vaśī krodhavivārjitaḥ //
1.22.d:
ततः प्रातः समुत्थाय नित्यकर्म समाप्य च ।
श्रद्धया पूजयेद्विष्णुं वशी क्रोधविवार्जितः ॥
1.22.m: Then, having risen in the morning and completed the daily rites, / self-controlled and free from anger, one should worship Viṣṇu with faith.

1.22.s:
vidvadbhiḥ sahito viṣṇumarcayitvā yathocitam /
saṃkalpaṃ tu tataḥ kuryāstvasti vācanapūrvakam //
1.22.d:
विद्वद्भिः सहितो विष्णुमर्चयित्वा यथोचितम् ।
संकल्पं तु ततः कुर्यास्त्वस्ति वाचनपूर्वकम् ॥
1.22.m: Having worshipped Viṣṇu properly in the company of learned men, / one should then make a solemn resolve (saṃkalpa) preceded by the recitation of blessings:

1.22.s:
māsamekaṃ nirāhāro hyadyaprabhṛti keśava /
māsāntaṃ pāraṇaṃ kurve devadeva tavājñayā //
1.22.d:
मासमेकं निराहारो ह्यद्यप्रभृति केशव ।
मासान्तं पारणं कुर्वे देवदेव तवाज्ञया ॥
1.22.m: “Remaining without food for one month from today onward, O Keśava, / at the end of the month I shall break my fast by your command, O god of gods!

1.22.s:
taporupa namastubhyaṃ tapasāṃ phala dāyaka /
mamābhūṣṭapradaṃ dehi sarvavinghānnivāraya //
1.22.d:
तपोरुप नमस्तुभ्यं तपसां फल दायक ।
ममाभूष्टप्रदं देहि सर्वविन्घान्निवारय ॥
1.22.m: Salutations to you whose form is austerity, O giver of the fruit of austerities! / Grant what is desired by me, and remove all obstacles!”

1.22.s:
evaṃ samarpya devasya viṣṇormāsavrataṃ śubham /
tataḥ prabhṛti māsāntaṃ nivaseddharimandire //
1.22.d:
एवं समर्प्य देवस्य विष्णोर्मासव्रतं शुभम् ।
ततः प्रभृति मासान्तं निवसेद्धरिमन्दिरे ॥
1.22.m: Having thus dedicated to the god Viṣṇu this auspicious month-long vow, / from that time until the end of the month one should reside in a temple of Hari.

1.22.s:
pratyahaṃ snāpayeddevaṃ pañcāmṛtavidhānataḥ /
dīpaṃ nirantaraṃ kuryāttasminmāse harergṛhe //
1.22.d:
प्रत्यहं स्नापयेद्देवं पञ्चामृतविधानतः ।
दीपं निरन्तरं कुर्यात्तस्मिन्मासे हरेर्गृहे ॥
1.22.m: Every day one should bathe the deity according to the rite of the fivefold nectar (pañcāmṛta); / one should keep a perpetual lamp burning in Hari's temple during that month.

1.22.s:
pratyahaṃ khādayetkāṣṭhaṃ hyapāmārga samudbhavam /
tataḥ snāyīta vidhinnārāyaṇaparāyaṇaḥ //
1.22.d:
प्रत्यहं खादयेत्काष्ठं ह्यपामार्ग समुद्भवम् ।
ततः स्नायीत विधिन्नारायणपरायणः ॥
1.22.m: Every day one should chew a tooth-stick derived from the apāmārga plant; / then one should bathe according to rule, dedicated to Nārāyaṇa.

1.22.s:
tataḥ saṃsnāpayedviṣṇuṃ pūrvavatprayator'cayet /
brāhmaṇānbhojayecchaktyā bhaktiyuktaḥ sada kṣiṇam //
1.22.d:
ततः संस्नापयेद्विष्णुं पूर्ववत्प्रयतोर्ऽचयेत् ।
ब्राह्मणान्भोजयेच्छक्त्या भक्तियुक्तः सद क्षिणम् ॥
1.22.m: Then, having bathed Viṣṇu, pure, one should worship him as before; / endowed with devotion, one should feed brāhmaṇas according to one's capacity, with a sacrificial fee,

1.22.s:
svayaṃ ca bandhubhiḥ sārddhaṃ bhuñjīta prayatendriyaḥ /
evaṃ māsopavāsāṃśca vratī kuryāt trayodaśa //
1.22.d:
स्वयं च बन्धुभिः सार्द्धं भुञ्जीत प्रयतेन्द्रियः ।
एवं मासोपवासांश्च व्रती कुर्यात् त्रयोदश ॥
1.22.m: and, with restrained senses, eat oneself along with one's kin. / In this way the observer of the vow should perform thirteen monthly fasts.

1.22.s:
varṣānte vedaviduṣe gāṃ pradadyātsa dakṣiṇām /
bhojayedvrāhmāṇāṃstatra dvādaśaiva vidhānataḥ /
śaktyā ca dakṣiṇāṃ dadyādrūhyaṇyābharaṇāni ca //
1.22.d:
वर्षान्ते वेदविदुषे गां प्रदद्यात्स दक्षिणाम् ।
भोजयेद्व्राह्माणांस्तत्र द्वादशैव विधानतः ।
शक्त्या च दक्षिणां दद्याद्रूह्यण्याभरणानि च ॥
1.22.m: At the end of the year, one should give a cow accompanied by a sacrificial fee to one learned in the Veda; / one should feed twelve brāhmaṇas there according to rule, / and according to ability one should give a sacrificial fee and ornaments.

1.22.s:
māsopavāsatritayaṃ yaḥ kuryātsaṃyate ndriyaḥ /
ātporyāmasya yajñatya dviguṇaṃ phalamaśnute //
1.22.d:
मासोपवासत्रितयं यः कुर्यात्संयते न्द्रियः ।
आत्पोर्यामस्य यज्ञत्य द्विगुणं फलमश्नुते ॥
1.22.m: Whoever, with restrained senses, observes a triad of month-long fasts, / obtains twice the fruit of the āptoryāma sacrifice.

1.22.s:
catuḥ kṛtvaḥ kṛtaṃ yena pārākaṃ munisattama /
sa labhetparamaṃ puṇyamaṣṭāngiṣṭomasaṃbhavam //
1.22.d:
चतुः कृत्वः कृतं येन पाराकं मुनिसत्तम ।
स लभेत्परमं पुण्यमष्टान्गिष्टोमसंभवम् ॥
1.22.m: He by whom this supreme fast (pārāka) is performed four times, O best of sages, / obtains the supreme merit arising from eight agniṣṭoma sacrifices.

1.22.s:
pañcakṛtvo vratamidaṃ kṛtaṃ yena mahātmanā /
atyangiṣṭomajaṃ puṇyaṃ dviguṇaṃ prāpnuyānnaraḥ //
1.22.d:
पञ्चकृत्वो व्रतमिदं कृतं येन महात्मना ।
अत्यन्गिष्टोमजं पुण्यं द्विगुणं प्राप्नुयान्नरः ॥
1.22.m:
A great-souled person by whom this vow has been performed five times
obtains double the merit born of the Atyagniṣṭoma sacrifice.

1.22.s:
māsopavāṣaṭkaṃ yaḥ karoti susamāhitaḥ /
jyotiṣṭo syanga yajñasya phalaṃ so 'ṣṭaguṇaṃ labhet //
1.22.d:
मासोपवाषट्कं यः करोति सुसमाहितः ।
ज्योतिष्टो स्यन्ग यज्ञस्य फलं सो ऽष्टगुणं लभेत् ॥
1.22.m:
He who, deeply concentrated, performs six month-long fasts,
shall obtain eightfold the fruit of the Jyotiṣṭoma sacrifice.

1.22.s:
nirāhāraḥ satpakṛtvo naro māsopavāsakān /
aśvamedhasya yajñasya phalamaṣṭaguṇaṃ labhet //
1.22.d:
निराहारः सत्पकृत्वो नरो मासोपवासकान् ।
अश्वमेधस्य यज्ञस्य फलमष्टगुणं लभेत् ॥
1.22.m:
A man without food through seven month-long fasts
shall obtain eightfold the fruit of the horse sacrifice.

1.22.s:
māso pāvāsānyaḥ kuryādaṣṭakṛtvo munīśvara /
naramedhākhyayajñasya phalaṃ pañcaguṇaṃ labhet //
1.22.d:
मासो पावासान्यः कुर्यादष्टकृत्वो मुनीश्वर ।
नरमेधाख्ययज्ञस्य फलं पञ्चगुणं लभेत् ॥
1.22.m:
He who should perform month-long fasts eight times, O lord of sages,
shall obtain fivefold the fruit of the sacrifice named the human sacrifice.

1.22.s:
yastu māsopavāsāṃśca navakṛtvaḥ samācaret /
gomedhamakhajaṃ puṇyaṃ labhate triguṇaṃ naraḥ //
1.22.d:
यस्तु मासोपवासांश्च नवकृत्वः समाचरेत् ।
गोमेधमखजं पुण्यं लभते त्रिगुणं नरः ॥
1.22.m:
And the man who should perform month-long fasts nine times
obtains threefold the merit born of the cow sacrifice.

1.22.s:
daśakṛtvastu yaḥ kuryātparākaṃ munisattama /
sa brahmamedhayajñasya triguṇaṃ phalamaśnute //
1.22.d:
दशकृत्वस्तु यः कुर्यात्पराकं मुनिसत्तम ।
स ब्रह्ममेधयज्ञस्य त्रिगुणं फलमश्नुते ॥
1.22.m:
He who should perform the Parāka ten times, O best of sages,
enjoys threefold the fruit of the Brahmamedha sacrifice.

1.22.s:
ekādaśa parākāṃśca yaḥ kuryātsaṃyatendriyaḥ /
sa yāti harisārupyaṃ sarvabhogasamanvitam //
1.22.d:
एकादश पराकांश्च यः कुर्यात्संयतेन्द्रियः ।
स याति हरिसारुप्यं सर्वभोगसमन्वितम् ॥
1.22.m:
And he who, with senses restrained, should perform eleven Parākas
attains sameness of form with Hari, endowed with all enjoyments.

1.22.s:
trayodaśa parākāṃśca yaḥ kuryātprayato naraḥ /
sa yāti paramānandaṃ yatra gatvā na śocati //
1.22.d:
त्रयोदश पराकांश्च यः कुर्यात्प्रयतो नरः ।
स याति परमानन्दं यत्र गत्वा न शोचति ॥
1.22.m:
And the self-controlled man who should perform thirteen Parākas
attains supreme bliss, having reached which he does not grieve.

1.22.s:
māsopavāsaniratā gaṅgāsnānaparāyaṇāḥ /
dhamamāgapravaktāro muktā eva na saśaṃyaḥ //
1.22.d:
मासोपवासनिरता गङ्गास्नानपरायणाः ।
धममागप्रवक्तारो मुक्ता एव न सशंयः ॥
1.22.m:
Those devoted to month-long fasts, dedicated to bathing in the Gaṅgā,
and proclaimers of the path of righteousness are liberated indeed, without doubt.

1.22.s:
avīrābhiryatibhirbrahyacāribhiḥ /
māsopavāsaḥ karttavyo vanasthaiśca viśeṣataḥ //
1.22.d:
अवीराभिर्यतिभिर्ब्रह्यचारिभिः ।
मासोपवासः कर्त्तव्यो वनस्थैश्च विशेषतः ॥
1.22.m:
By childless women, ascetics, celibate students,
and especially by forest-dwellers, a month-long fast should be undertaken.

1.22.s:
nārī vā puruṣo vāpi vratametatsudurlabham /
kṛtvā mokṣamavānpoti yogināmapi durlabham //
1.22.d:
नारी वा पुरुषो वापि व्रतमेतत्सुदुर्लभम् ।
कृत्वा मोक्षमवान्पोति योगिनामपि दुर्लभम् ॥
1.22.m:
A woman or a man, having performed this very difficult-to-obtain vow,
attains liberation, which is hard to obtain even for yogins.

1.22.s:
gṛhastho vānaprastho vā vratī vā bhikṣureva vā /
mūrkho vā paṇḍito vāpi śrutvaitanmokṣabhāgbhavet //
1.22.d:
गृहस्थो वानप्रस्थो वा व्रती वा भिक्षुरेव वा ।
मूर्खो वा पण्डितो वापि श्रुत्वैतन्मोक्षभाग्भवेत् ॥
1.22.m:
A householder, a forest-dweller, an observer of vows, or a mendicant,
a fool or a learned person, upon hearing this, becomes an enjoyer of liberation.

1.22.s:
idaṃ puṇyaṃ vratākhyānaṃ nārāyaṇa parāyaṇaḥ /
śṛṇuyādvācayedvāpi sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate //
iti śrībṛhannāradīyapurāṇe pūrvabhāge prathamapāde vratākhyāne māsopavāsavarṇanaṃ nāma dvādaśo 'dhyāyaḥ
1.22.d:
इदं पुण्यं व्रताख्यानं नारायण परायणः ।
शृणुयाद्वाचयेद्वापि सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते ॥
इति श्रीबृहन्नारदीयपुराणे पूर्वभागे प्रथमपादे व्रताख्याने मासोपवासवर्णनं नाम द्वादशो ऽध्यायः
1.22.m:
Dedicated to Nārāyaṇa, whoever hears or causes this sacred narrative of the vow to be read
is freed from all sins.

Thus ends the twelfth chapter, entitled 'Description of the Month-Long Fast in the Narrative of Vows', in the first quarter of the first part of the glorious Bṛhannāradīya Purāṇa.
